definition: He did it previously, or beforehand.
sourceDefinition: He did it previously, or beforehand. (O and TA in art. zlf .) ― -b2- [Hence,] Aslf fiY , ka*aA , (S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) inf. n. A_isolaAfN ; (TA;) and fiyhi ↓ sl~f , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) inf. n. tasoliyfN ; (Msb, TA;) He paid in advance, or beforehand, for such a thing, (S, Mgh, TA,) i. e. a commodity described to him, (S,) or wheat or the like, for which the seller became responsible, [ with something additional to the equivalent of the current price at the time of the payment, (see salafN ,)] (TA,) to be delivered at a certain period: (S:) and A^asolama signifies the same. (TA.) You say, A^asolafotu A_ilayohi fiY ka*aA and A_ilayohi ↓ sal~afotu [ I paid in advance to him for such a thing, &c.]. (Msb.) Hence the saying in a trad., fayusal~ifo ↓ mano sal~afa fiY kayolK maEoluwmK wawazonK maEoluwmK A_ilaY A^ajalK maEoluwmK i. e. He who pays in advance for a commodity for which the seller is responsible, let him pay in advance for a certain measure, and a certain weight, to be delivered at a certain period. (TA.) ― -b3- And Aslfhu maAlFA , (S, M, Mgh, TA,) and ↓ sl~fhu , (M, Mgh, TA,) He lent him property [ to be repaid, or returned, without any profit ]. (M, Mgh, TA. [See, again, salafN .]) [Whence one says, Aslfhu A_iHosaAnFA and sl~fhu , and ↓ sl~fhu , meaning (assumed tropical:) He did to him, to be requited it, a good action and an evil action; as is shown by the words maA A^asolafota mino A_isaA='apK A^awo A_iHosaAnK wamaA tuEoTiyhi lituqoDaAhu in art. qrD in the K, and by the corresponding words maA sal~afota mino A_iHosaAnK wamino A_isaA='apK in the same art. in the S: see also Bd in xxxvi. 11: and see zal~afahu . And hence,] a poet says, AljaAra $irobFA wahoYa HaAy^imapN ↓ tusal~ifu waAlmaA='u lazonN bakiYo'u AlEayoni muqotasamu (assumed tropical:) [ They (referring to camels) yield promptly to the neighbour a draught of milk, while they are thirsty, and going round about the water, when the water is crowded upon, scanty in the source, divided by lot ]. (TA. [See also some verses of El-Akra' Ibn-Mo'ádh, in which the former hemistich occurs with a different latter hemistich, in the Ham p. 753.]) -A2- See also 1, last sentence but one.

definition: Such as have gone before, or preceded;
sourceDefinition: Such as have gone before, or preceded; (M, Msb; *) [i. e. the preceding generations; ] as also ↓ saliyfN and ↓ sulofapN and ↓ saluwfN ; all quasipl. ns.; (M;) of which the sing. is ↓ saAlifN : (M, Msb: *) or such as have gone before, or preceded, of a man's ancestors (S, K) and of his relations, (K,) that are above him in age and in excellence; [but this addition is not always agreeable with usage;] one of whom is termed ↓ saAlifN : (TA:) the pl. of salafN is A^asolaAfN and sul~aAfN , (S, K,) [the former a pl. of pauc. and the latter of mult.,] or the latter is pl. of ↓ saAlifN , and so is salafN [said to be, though this is more properly termed, as it is in the M, a quasi-pl. n.]: (IB, Msb, TA:) and, accord. to Zj, sulufN is pl. of ↓ saliyfN , and sulafN is pl. of ↓ sulofapN , which means a company ( EuSobapN ) that has passed away: (M:) or ↓ saAlifN and ↓ saliyfN signify the same; going before; preceding; syn. mutaqad~imN . (S.) [Accord. to Abu-lMahásin, Als~alafu is particularly applied to 'Áïsheh the wife of Mohammad, the three Khaleefehs Aboo-Bekr and 'Omar and 'Othmán, Talhah and Ez-Zubeyr, the Khaleefeh Mo'áwiyeh, and 'Amr Ibn-El-Ás. (De Sacy's Chrest. Ar., sec. ed., i. 156.)] And Als~alafu AlS~aAliHu is applied to the first chief persons of the Tábi'ees. (TA.) And Als~alafu Almuqad~amu is an appellation of the prophet Mohammad. (Ham p. 780.) [Hence, ma*aAhibu Als~alafi The tenets of the early Muslims. ] ― -b2- Also A people, or party, going before, or preceding, in journeying. (TA.) ― -b3- And [simply] A company of men; as in the saying, jaA='aniY salafN mina Aln~aAsi [ A company of men came to me ]. (M.) ― -b4- And Any good, or righteous, deed, that one has done beforehand [ by way of preparing a future reward ]: or any faraT [i. e. cause of reward, or recompense, in the world to come, such as a child dying in infancy ], that [ as it were ] goes before one. (A 'Obeyd, O, K.) ― -b5- And i. q. salamN ; (T, Hr, Mgh, O, K, TA;) i. e. Any money, or property, paid in advance, or beforehand, as the price of a commodity for which the seller has become responsible and which one has bought on description: (T, TA:) or payment for a commodity to be delivered at a certain [ future ] period with something additional to [ the equivalent of ] the current price at the time of such payment; this [transaction] being a cause of profit to him who makes such payment; and salamN also has this meaning: (TA:) or a sort of sale in which the price is paid in advance, and the commodity is withheld, on the condition of description, to a certain [ future ] period: (S, O:) it is a subst. from AlA_isolaAfu . (Msb, * K, TA.) ― -b6- And A loan ( qaroDN ) in which is no profit (Hr, O, Mgh, K, TA) to the lender (Hr, O, K, TA) except recompense [ in the world to come ] and thanks, (TA,) and which it is incumbent on the recipient thereof to return as he received it: (Hr, O, K, TA:) thus the Arabs term it: (Hr, O, TA:) and in this sense also the word is a subst. from AlA_isolaAfu . (TA.) -A2- Also A stallion-camel. sourceDefinition: (tropical:) Two ducts ( EiroqaAni ) in the two nostrils, (S, K, *) in the inside, (TA,) which, when an ass is excited by lust, flow with water, (S, TA,) or with blood: (TA:) so in the verse of Esh-Shemmákh, tuwaAy^ilu mino miSak~K A^anoSabatohu HawaAlibu A^asoharayohi biAl*~aniyni [ She seeks to escape from a strong ( he-ass ) whom the ducts of his two nostrils flowing with mucus have fatigued ]: (S:) or the nose and the penis: (Sh, K:) or (TA, but in the K “ and ”) two ducts in the flesh and sinew next the back-bone, through which runs the seminal fluid into the penis: (K:) or (TA) two ducts rising from the two testicles, and meeting together in the interior of the penis, (K,) or of the fayo$alap [or glans of the penis ]; which are the ducts of the seminal fluid: (TA:) or the two veins or ducts of the penis which become prominent when it is in a state of erection: (TA:) and two veins or ducts in the eye: (K:) but As disallows Ashryh , and says that the true reading, in the verse of Esh-Shemmákh, is A^asoharatohu , meaning, [ that ] have not suffered him to sleep. (TA.) [See also HaAlibN .]

definition: , (S, K,) or Aln~aEama , (Mgh,) or Ald~aAb~apa , (Msb,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) or Aln~aEama , (Mgh,) or Ald~aAb~apa , (Msb,) aor. yasuwqu , (S, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. sawoqN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and siyaAqN , (S, [so in both of my copies, but it is said in the JK that this latter is used in relation to death, and such is generally the case,]) or sayaAqN , like saHaAbN , (TA, [but this I have not found elsewhere, and I doubt its correctness,]) and siyaAqapN and masaAqN , (O, K, TA,) He drove the cattle [or the beast ]; he urged the cattle [or the beast ] to go; (Mgh;) and ↓ AstAqhA signifies the same, (S, K,) as also ↓ AsAqhA , and ↓ sw~qhA ; (TA;) or tasowiyqN , the inf. n. [or this last], signifies the driving well: (KL:) [and accord. to Freytag, ↓ AstsAq , followed by an accus., signifies the same as saAqa as expl. above; but for this he names no authority.] Hence, in the Kur [lxxv. 30], A_ilaY rab~ika yawomay^i*K AlmasaAqu (TA) i. e. To thy Lord, and his judgment, on that day, shall be the driving. (Bd, Jel.) And the saying, in a trad., laAtaquwmu Als~aAEapu Hat~aY yaxoruja rajulN mino qaHoTaAna yasuwqu Aln~aAsa biEaSFAhu [properly rendered The resurrection, or the hour thereof, shall not come to pass until a man come forth from the tribe of Kahtán driving the people with his staff ], allusive to his having the mastery over them, and their obeying him; the staff being mentioned only to indicate his tyrannical and rough treatment of them. (TA.) [And hence the saying, sAq EalaY~a fulaAnFA (assumed tropical:) He urged such a one to intercede for him with me. ] ― -b2- [Hence also,] saAqahu Alqadaru A_ilaY maA qud~ira lahu (assumed tropical:) [ Destiny drove him, or impelled him, to that which was destined for him ]. (TA.) [And in like manner one says of desire, &c.] ― -b3- And sAq A_ilaY AlmaroA^api mahorahaA , (K,) or SadaAqahaA , (S, Msb,) inf. n. siyaAqN ; (TA;) and ↓ AsAqhu ; (Msb, K;) (tropical:) He sent to the woman her dowry; (K, TA;) or conveyed it, or caused it to be conveyed, to her; (Msb;) though consisting of dirhems or deenárs; because the dowry, with the Arabs, originally consisted of camels, which are driven. (TA.) And hence, maAsuqota A_ilayohaA , meaning (assumed tropical:) What didst thou give her as her dowry? occurring in a trad.; or, as some related it, maA suqota minohaA , i. e. What didst thou give for her, or in exchange for her? (TA.) And sAq A_ilayohi Al$~aYo'a (assumed tropical:) [ He made, or caused, the thing to go, pass, or be conveyed or transmitted, to him; he sent to him the thing ]. (M and K in art. AtY .) And sAq A_ilayohi xayorFA (tropical:) [ He caused good, or good fortune, to betide him ]. (TA.) And sAq liA^aroDihi A^atiy~FA (assumed tropical:) [ He made a rivulet, or a channel for water, to run to his land ], (M in art. AtY .) ― -b4- [Hence likewise,] saAqati Alr~iyHu Als~aHaAba (tropical:) [ The wind drove along the clouds ]. (S, * TA.) ― -b5- [And sAq AlHadiyva , inf. n. siyaAqN and sawoqN and masaAqN , (tropical:) He carried on the narrative, or discourse. ] You say, fulaAnN yasuwqu AlHadiyva A^aHosana siyaAqK (tropical:) [ Such a one carries on the narrative, or discourse, in the best manner of doing so ]. (Mgh, TA.) And A_ilayoka yusaAqu AlHadiyvu (tropical:) [ To thee as its object the narrative, or discourse, is carried on ]. (TA.) And kalaAmN masaAquhu A_ilaY ka*aA (tropical:) [ Speech whereof the carrying-on is pointed to such a thing ]. (TA.) And jiy^otuka biAlHadiyvi EalaY sawoqihi (tropical:) [ I uttered to thee the narrative, or discourse, after the proper manner of the carrying-on thereof ]. (TA.) [In like manner also one says,] sAq AlA^umuwra A^aHosana masaAqK (assumed tropical:) [ He carried on, or prosecuted, affairs, or the affairs, in the best manner of doing so ]. (A in art. Hw* .) ― -b6- sawoqu AlmaEoluwmi masaAqa gayorihi [from sAq AlHadiyva expl. above] means (assumed tropical:) The asking respecting that which one knows in the manner of one's asking respecting that which he knows not: a mode of speech implying hyperbole: as when one says, A^awajohuka h`*aA A^amo badorN [ Is this thy face or a full moon? ]. (Kull p. 211.) ― -b7- sAq said of a sick man, (K,) and sAq nafosahu , [app. thus originally,] (Ks, Msb, TA,) and sAq binafosihi , (TA,) aor. yasuwqu , (Ks, S, O, Msb, TA,) inf. n. siyaAqN , (S, O, Msb, K,) originally siwaAqN , (TA,) and sawoqN (O, K) and suw^uwqN , (TA,) (tropical:) He cast forth, or vomited, his soul; (Ks, TA;) he gave up his spirit; or was at the point of death, in the agony of death, or at the point of having his soul drawn forth; (S, O, Msb, TA;) or he began to give up his spirit, or to have his soul drawn forth. (K.) You say, raA^ayotu fulaAnFA yasuwqu (tropical:) I saw such a one giving up his spirit at death. (S, O, TA.) And raA^ayotu fulaAnFA biAls~awoqi [or fiY Als~iyaAqi , as in the Msb,] (tropical:) I saw such a one in the act [or agony ] of death; and yusaAqu [ having his soul expelled ], inf. n. sawoqN : and A_in~a nafosahu latusaAqu (tropical:) [ Verily his soul is being expelled ]. (ISh, TA.) -A2- saAqahu , (K,) first pers. suqotuhu , (S,) aor. as above, inf. n. sawoqN , (TA,) also signifies He hit, or hurt, his (another man's, S) saAq [or shank ]. (S, K.)

definition: He vied, or competed, with him, in driving: (K: [in the CK, for fY Als~awoqi , is put fY Als~uwoqi :]) or he vied, or competed, with him to decide which of them twain was the stronger;
sourceDefinition: He vied, or competed, with him, in driving: (K: [in the CK, for fY Als~awoqi , is put fY Als~uwoqi :]) or he vied, or competed, with him to decide which of them twain was the stronger; from the phrase qaAmati AlHarobu EalaY saAqK . (S.) [Hence,] one says baEiyrN yusaAwiqu AlS~ayoda (tropical:) [ A camel that vies with the animals of the chase in driving on, or in strength ]. (JK, Ibn-'Abbád, O, K, TA.) ― -b2- musaAwaqapN is also syn. with mutaAbaEapN [app. as meaning (assumed tropical:) The making to be consecutive, or successive, for it is added], as though driving on one another, or as though one portion were driving on another. (TA. [See 6, its quasi-pass.].) ― -b3- [Freytag also assigns to sAwq the meaning of He, or it, followed ( secutus fuit ), as on the authority of the Hamáseh; but without pointing out the page; and it is not in his index of words explained therein.]

The lawyers say, tsAwqt AlxiTobataAni , meaning (tropical:) [ The two demandings of a woman in marriage ] were simultaneous: but [Fei says] I have not found it in the books of lexicology in this sense. (Msb.)

definition: The shank; i. e. the part between the knee and the foot of a human being; (Msb;) or the part between the ankle and the knee (K, TA) of a human being; (TA;) the sAq of the human foot: (S, TA:) and...
sourceDefinition: The shank; i. e. the part between the knee and the foot of a human being; (Msb;) or the part between the ankle and the knee (K, TA) of a human being; (TA;) the sAq of the human foot: (S, TA:) and [the part properly corresponding thereto, i. e. the thigh commonly so called, and also the arm, of a beast;] the part above the waZiyf of the horse and mule and ass and camel, and the part above the kuraAE of the ox-kind and sheep or goat and antelope: (TA:) [it is also sometimes applied to the shank commonly so called, of the hind leg, and, less properly, of the fore leg, of a beast: and to the bone of any of the parts above mentioned: and sometimes, by synecdoche, to the hind leg, and, less properly, to the fore leg also, of a beast: it generally corresponds to *iraAEN : of a bird, it is the thigh commonly so called: and sometimes the shank commonly so called: and, by synecdoche, the leg: ] it is of the fem. gender: (Msb, TA:) and for this reason, (TA,) the dim. is ↓ suwayoqapN : (Msb, TA:) the pl. [of mult.] is suwqN (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and siyqaAnN and [of pauc.] A^asow^uqN , (S, O, K,) the w in this last being with ' in order that it may bear the dammeh. (O, K.) A poet says, lilofataY EaqolN yaEiy$u bihi Hayovu tahodiY saAqahu qadamuho meaning The young man has intelligence whereby he lives when his foot directs aright his shank. (IAar, TA.) And one says of a man when difficulty, or calamity, befalls him, ka$afa Eano saAqihi [lit. He uncovered his shank; meaning (assumed tropical:) he prepared himself for difficulty ]: so says IAmb: and hence, he says, (TA, [in which a similar explanation is cited from ISd also,]) they mention the sAq when they mean to express the difficulty of a case or an event, and to tell of the terror occasioned thereby. (K, TA.) Thus, the saying yawoma yuko$afu Eano saAqK , (S, K, TA,) in the Kur [lxviii. 42], (S, TA,) [lit. On a day when a shank shall be uncovered, ] means (assumed tropical:) on a day when difficulty, or calamity, shall be disclosed. (I'Ab, Mujáhid, S, K, TA.) It is like the saying, qaAmati AlHarobu EalaY saAqK , (S, TA,) which means (assumed tropical:) The war, or battle, became vehement, (Msb in this art. and in art. Hrb ,) so that safety from destruction was difficult of attainment: (Id. in art. Hrb :) and ka$afati AlHarobu Eano saAqK , [as also $am~arato Eano saAqihaA ,] i. e. (assumed tropical:) The war, or battle, became vehement. (Jel in lxviii. 42.) And in like manner, waA@lotaf~ati A@ls~aAqu biAls~aAqi , (K, TA,) in the Kur [lxxv. 29], (TA,) means (assumed tropical:) And the affliction of the present state of existence shall be combined with that of the final state: (K, TA:) or it means when the [one] leg shall be inwrapped with the other leg by means of the grave-clothes. (TA.) One says also, qaAma Alqawomu EalaY saAqK (assumed tropical:) The people or party, became in a state of toil, and trouble, or distress. (TA.) And qaraEa liloA^amori saAqahu , [originating from one's striking the shin of his camel in order to make him lie down to be mounted; lit. He struck his shank for the affair; ] meaning (assumed tropical:) he prepared himself for the thing, or affair; syn. ta$am~ara : (JK:) or he was, or became, light, or active, and he rose, or hastened, to do the thing; or (assumed tropical:) he applied himself vigorously, or diligently, or with energy, to the thing, or affair; i. q. $am~ara lahu [q. v.]; (TA;) or tajar~ada lahu . (A and TA in art. qrE [q. v.: see also ZunobuwbN , in several places].) [It is also said that] A^awohato bisaAqK means kidotu A^afoEalu [i. e. I nearly, or almost, did what I purposed: but this explanation seems to have been derived only from what here, as in the TA, immediately follows]: Kurt says, describing the wolf, wal`kin~iY ramayotuka mino baEiydK falamo A^afoEalo waqado A^awohato bisaAqi [i. e., app., But I shot at thee from afar, and I did not what I purposed, though it (the shot, Alr~amoyapu , I suppose, being meant to be understood,) maimed a shank: which virtually means, though I nearly did what I purposed: the poet, I assume, says Awht bsAq for the sake of the measure and rhyme, for A^awohato saAqFA : see what is said, in the explanations of the preposition bi , respecting the phrase waA@mosaHuwA biruw^u=sikumo ]. (TA.) ― -b2- By a secondary application, saAqN signifies (assumed tropical:) [ A greave; i. e.] a thing that is worn on the sAq [or shank ] of the leg, made of iron or other material. (Mgh.) ― -b3- Also (tropical:) [The stem, stock, or trunk, i. e.] the part between the A^aSol [here meaning root, or foot, (though it is also syn. with sAq in the sense in which the latter is here explained,)] and the place where the branches shoot out; (TA;) or the support; (Msb;) or the ji*oE ; (S, K;) of a tree, or shrub: (S, Msb, K, TA:) pl. [of mult.] suwqN (Msb, TA) and suwqN and suwuwqN and suw^uwqN and [of pauc.] A^asowuqN and A^asow^uqN . (TA.) It is related in a trad. of Mo'áwiyeh, that a man said, I applied to him to decide in a litigation with the son of my brother, and began to overcome him therein; whereupon he said, Thou art like as Aboo-Duwád says, A^an~aY A^utiyHa lahu HirobaA='u tanoDubapK laA yurosilu Als~aAqa A_il~aA mumosikFA saAqaA [ Whencesoever, or however, a preparation is made for him, to catch him, he is like a chameleon of a tree of the kind called tanoDub , he will not loose the stem thereof unless grasping a stem ]: he meant that no plea of his came to nought but he clung to another; likening him to the chameleon, which places itself facing the sun, and ascends half-way up the tree, or shrub, then climbs to the branches when the sun becomes hot, then climbs to a higher branch, and will not loose the former until it grasps the other. (O, TA. *) ― -b4- [Hence, perhaps, as it seems to be indicated in the O,] one says, waladato fulaAnapu valaAvapa baniyna EalaY saAqK , (K, [in the copies of which, however, I find valaAva put for valaAvapa ,]) or EalaY saAqK waAHidK , (S,) or waAHidapK , (O,) i. e. (tropical:) Such a woman brought forth three sons, one after another, without any girl between them: (S, O, K, TA:) so says ISk: and wulida lifulaAnK valaAvapu A^awolaAdK saAqFA EalaY saAqK , i. e. (tropical:) Three children were born to such a one, one after another. (TA.) And banaY Alqawomu buyuwtahumo EalaY saAqK waAHidK (assumed tropical:) [ The people, or party, built their houses, or constructed their tents, in one row or series ]. (TA.) ― -b5- saAqN also signifies (assumed tropical:) The soul, or self; syn. nafosN : hence the saying of 'Alee (in the war of the [schismatics called] $uraAp ), laAbud~a liY mino qitaAlihimo walawo talifato saAqiY (assumed tropical:) [ There is not for me any way of avoiding combating them, though my soul, or self, should perish by my doing so]. (Abu-l-' Abbás, O, TA.) So too in the saying, qadaHa fiY saAqihi [as though meaning (tropical:) He cankered his very soul ]: (IAar, TA in art. qdH :) [or] he deceived him, and did that which was displeasing to him: (L in that art.:) or (tropical:) he impugned his honour, or reputation; from the action of canker-worms ( qawaAdiH ) cankering the stem, or trunk, of a shrub, or tree. (A in that art.) -A2- saAqu Hur~K [is said to signify] The male of the qamaAriY~ [or species of collared turtle-doves of which the female is called qumoriy~apN (see qumoriY~N )]; (S, Msb, K;) i. e. the wara$aAn : (S, Msb:) the former appellation being given to it as imitative of its cry: (As, K:) it has neither fem. nor pl.: (AHát, TA:) or Als~aAqu is the pigeon; and AlHur~u , its young one: (Sh, K:) the poet Ibn-Harmeh uses the phrase kasaAqi A@boni Hur~K . (O, TA.) [See more in art. Hr .]

definition: [ A market, mart, or fair;
sourceDefinition: [ A market, mart, or fair; ] a place in which commerce is carried on; (ISd, Msb, TA;) a place of articles of merchandise: (Mgh, TA:) so called because people drive their commodities thither: (TA:) [in the S unexplained, and in the K only said to be well-known:] of the fem. gender, and masc., (S, Mgh, Msb, K, *) the former in the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz, and the latter in that of Temeem, (S and Msb voce zuqaAqN , q. v.,) the former the more chaste, or the making it masc. is a mistake: (Msb:) pl. A^asowaAqN : (TA:) the dim. is ↓ suwayoqapN [with p , confirming the opinion of those who hold suwqN to be only fem.]: also signifying merchandise, syn. tijaArapN ; as in the phrase, jaA'ato suwayoqapN [ Merchandise came ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] suwqu AlHarobi (tropical:) The thickest, or most vehement part ( Hawomap ) of the fight; (S, K, TA;) and so AlHarobi ↓ suwqapu ; i. e. the midst thereof. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: Meal of parched barley ( $aEiyr ), or of [ the species thereof, or similar grain, called ] sulot , likewise parched; and it is also of wheat; but is mostly made of barley ( $Eyr ); (MF, TA;) what is made of wheat or of barley; (Msb, TA;) well known: (S, Msb, K, TA:) [it is generally made into a kind of gruel, or thick ptisan, being moistened with water, or clarified butter, or fat of a sheep's tail, &c.; (see lat~a ;) and is therefore said (in the Msb in art. sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K, &c.,) aor. , (A, K,) inf. n. $urobN and $arobN (S, A, Msb, K, &c.) and $irobN , (S, A, K,) agreeably with three different readings of the Kur lvi. 55, (S, TA,) the first of which (with damm) is that generally obtaining, (Fr, TA,) and is the only one admitted by Jaafar Ibn-Mohammad, notwithstanding which the second form (with fet-h) is said by MF to be the most chaste as well as the most agreeable with analogy, (TA,) or the second (with fet-h) is an inf. n., and the first is a simple subst., (AO, S, Msb, K,) and so is the third, (AO, S, K,) and ma$orabN , (S, K,) which is also a n. of place [and of time], (S,) and ta$oraAbN , (S K, TA,) a form used when muchness of the act is meant, (TA,) and ti$oraAbN , which is anomalous, (TA voce bay~ana , q. v.,) He drank, (KL, PS, TK,) or he swallowed, syn. jariEa , (A, K, [but the former meaning is evidently intended by this explanation, and such I shall assume to be the case in giving the explanations of the derivatives in the A and K. &c.,]) water, &c., (S,) or a liquid, properly by sucking in, or sipping; and otherwise tropically; (Msb;) [generally, gulping it; for] you say, $ariba AlmaA='a fiY kar~apK [ He drank the water at once, or at a single draught ]; and fiY ↓ t$r~bhu muholapK [ He drank it leisurely, or gently, or slowly ]: (Mgh:) $urobN signifies the conveying to one's inside, by means of his mouth, that in the case of which chewing is not practicable: (KT:) [but] Es-Sarakustee says, one does not say of a bird $ariba AlmaA='a , but HasaAhu . (Msb.) In the saying of Aboo-Dhu-eyb, describing clouds, $aribona bimaA='i AlbaHori vum~a taraf~aEato [which is evidently best rendered They drank of the water of the sea, then rose aloft, agreeably with what has been stated respecting bi in the sense of mino in p. 143, it is said that] the b is redundant, or, as rawiyna is rendered trans. by means of bi , [though I do not think that this is the case unless bi be used as meaning “ by means of, ” and I do not remember to have met with an instance of it,] $aribona is thus rendered trans. (TA.) [See a similar ex. in the 28th verse of the Mo'allakah of 'Antarah, EM p. 232. One says also, $ariba fiY A_inaA='K , meaning He drank out of a vessel; agreeably with an explanation of mi$orabapN , in the S and K, as meaning A_inaA='N yu$orabu fiyhi .] And one says, A_in~iY laA^amokuvu Alyawomayoni maA A^a$orabuhumaA maA='F , meaning maA A^a$orabu fiyhimaA maA='F [i. e. Verily I tarry the two days not drinking in them water ]. (O.) ― -b2- [ $ariba Ald~awaA='a , in the conventional language of the physicians, as is indicated in the Mgh, voce banojN (q. v.), on the phrase $ariba Albanoja , and as is shown in many instances in the K &c., means He took, i. e. swallowed, the medicine, whether fluid or solid. ― -b3- And in the present day, they say, $ariba Ald~uxaAna , meaning He inhaled, properly imbibed, smoke of tobacco; or he smoked tobacco, or the tobacco. ] ― -b4- One says of seed-produce, or corn, when its culms have come forth, qado $ariba Alz~aroEu fiY AlqaSabi (assumed tropical:) [ The seed-produce, or corn, has imbibed into the culms ]: (O, TA:) and when the sap ( AlmaA=' ) has come into it, $ariba qaSabu Alz~aroEi (assumed tropical:) [ The culms of the seed-produce, or corn, have imbibed ]. (TA.) And one says, $ariba Als~unobulu Ald~aqiyqa (tropical:) [ The ears of corn imbibed the farina; or] became pervaded by the farina; (En-Nadr, A, O;) or had in them the alimentary substance; as though the farina were water which they drank. (TA.) And waqado $ariba Alz~aroEu Ald~aqiyqa , occurring in the story of Ohod, (O, TA,) as some relate it, or ↓ $ur~iba as others relate it, means (tropical:) [ And the seed-produce, or corn, had imbibed, or had been made to imbibe, the farina, or] had become hardened in its grain, and near to maturity. (TA.) [And ↓ A^u$oriba means the same: for one says,] A^u$oriba Alz~aroEu (tropical:) [ The seed-produce, or corn, was made to imbibe the farina; or] became pervaded by the farina: and in like manner, A^u$oriba Alz~aroEu Ald~aqiyqa , i. e. (tropical:) [ The seed-produce, or corn, was made to imbibe the farina, or] its alimentary substance. (TA.) ― -b5- One also says, A^akala ganamiY wa$aribahaA (tropical:) [ He ate the flesh of my sheep, or goats, and drank the milk of them ]. (TA in art. Akl .) And [in like manner] A^akala fulaAnN maAliY wa$aribahu (tropical:) [ Such a one fed upon, devoured, or consumed, my property ]. (A.) And A^akala Ealayohi Ald~ahoru wa$ariba (tropical:) [ Time wasted him, or wore him away; as though it fed upon him]. (A.) ― -b6- And maA lamo ↓ A^a$orabotaniY A^a$orabo [lit. Thou hast made me to drink what I have not drunk, ] meaning (tropical:) thou hast charged against me, or accused me of doing, what I have not done; (S, A, K;) like A^ak~alotaniY maA lamo A=kulo . (S in art. Akl .) ― -b7- $ariba also signifies He was, or became, satisfied with drinking: (TA:) and in like manner $aribat is said of camels. (A 'Obeyd, S, TA.) And He was, or became, thirsty; (K, TA;) thus having two contr. significations; (TA;) as also ↓ A^a$oraba . (K, TA.) ― -b8- Also, and ↓ A^a$oraba , His camels were, or became, satisfied with drinking: and, i. e. both these verbs, his camels were, or became, thirsty: (K, TA:) or the former verb signifies, or signifies also, (accord. to different copies of the K,) his camel was, or became, weak. (K, TA.) -A2- $ariba bihi , and bihi ↓ A^a$oraba , He lied against him. (K.) -A3- $araba , aor. , (O, K, TA,) inf. n. $arobN , (O, TA,) He understood: (O, K, TA:) on the authority of AA. (TA.) [In a copy of the A, the verb in this sense is written $ariba ; and app. not through the fault of the transcriber, for it is there mentioned as tropical: but in the O, it is said to be like kataba , aor. , inf. n. katobN ; and in the K, to be like naSara .] One says, $araba maA A^uloqiYa A_ilayohi , i. e. He understood [ what was told to him ]. (TA.) And one says to a stupid person, AuHolubo vum~a A@$orubo Kneel thou; then understand. (O, TA. See also 1 in art. Hlb .)

rawSourceText: , (S, A, K, &c.,) aor. , (A, K,) inf. n. $urobN and $arobN (S, A, Msb, K, &c.) and $irobN , (S, A, K,) agreeably with three different readings of the Kur lvi. 55, (S, TA,) the first of which (with damm) is that generally obtaining, (Fr, TA,) and is the only one admitted by Jaafar Ibn-Mohammad, notwithstanding which the second form (with fet-h) is said by MF to be the most chaste as well as the most agreeable with analogy, (TA,) or the second (with fet-h) is an inf. n., and the first is a simple subst., (AO, S, Msb, K,) and so is the third, (AO, S, K,) and ma$orabN , (S, K,) which is also a n. of place [and of time], (S,) and ta$oraAbN , (S K, TA,) a form used when muchness of the act is meant, (TA,) and ti$oraAbN , which is anomalous, (TA voce bay~ana , q. v.,) He drank, (KL, PS, TK,) or he swallowed, syn. jariEa , (A, K, [but the former meaning is evidently intended by this explanation, and such I shall assume to be the case in giving the explanations of the derivatives in the A and K. &c.,]) water, &c., (S,) or a liquid, properly by sucking in, or sipping; and otherwise tropically; (Msb;) [generally, gulping it; for] you say, $ariba AlmaA='a fiY kar~apK [ He drank the water at once, or at a single draught ]; and fiY ↓ t$r~bhu muholapK [ He drank it leisurely, or gently, or slowly ]: (Mgh:) $urobN signifies the conveying to one's inside, by means of his mouth, that in the case of which chewing is not practicable: (KT:) [but] Es-Sarakustee says, one does not say of a bird $ariba AlmaA='a , but HasaAhu . (Msb.) In the saying of Aboo-Dhu-eyb, describing clouds, $aribona bimaA='i AlbaHori vum~a taraf~aEato [which is evidently best rendered They drank of the water of the sea, then rose aloft, agreeably with what has been stated respecting bi in the sense of mino in p. 143, it is said that] the b is redundant, or, as rawiyna is rendered trans. by means of bi , [though I do not think that this is the case unless bi be used as meaning “ by means of, ” and I do not remember to have met with an instance of it,] $aribona is thus rendered trans. (TA.) [See a similar ex. in the 28th verse of the Mo'allakah of 'Antarah, EM p. 232. One says also, $ariba fiY A_inaA='K , meaning He drank out of a vessel; agreeably with an explanation of mi$orabapN , in the S and K, as meaning A_inaA='N yu$orabu fiyhi .] And one says, A_in~iY laA^amokuvu Alyawomayoni maA A^a$orabuhumaA maA='F , meaning maA A^a$orabu fiyhimaA maA='F [i. e. Verily I tarry the two days not drinking in them water ]. (O.) ― -b2- [ $ariba Ald~awaA='a , in the conventional language of the physicians, as is indicated in the Mgh, voce banojN (q. v.), on the phrase $ariba Albanoja , and as is shown in many instances in the K &c., means He took, i. e. swallowed, the medicine, whether fluid or solid. ― -b3- And in the present day, they say, $ariba Ald~uxaAna , meaning He inhaled, properly imbibed, smoke of tobacco; or he smoked tobacco, or the tobacco. ] ― -b4- One says of seed-produce, or corn, when its culms have come forth, qado $ariba Alz~aroEu fiY AlqaSabi (assumed tropical:) [ The seed-produce, or corn, has imbibed into the culms ]: (O, TA:) and when the sap ( AlmaA=' ) has come into it, $ariba qaSabu Alz~aroEi (assumed tropical:) [ The culms of the seed-produce, or corn, have imbibed ]. [And ↓ A^u$oriba means the same: for one says,] A^u$oriba Alz~aroEu (tropical:) [ The seed-produce, or corn, was made to imbibe the farina; or] became pervaded by the farina: and in like manner, A^u$oriba Alz~aroEu Ald~aqiyqa , i. e. (tropical:) [ The seed-produce, or corn, was made to imbibe the farina, or] its alimentary substance. Ai$oriy^obaAbN , (S, O,) (tropical:) He raised his head like the camel that has satisfied his thirst on the occasion of drinking: (A:) or he stretched forth his neck to look: (S, A, O, K:) not improbably, from Al$~urobu in its well known sense, as though he did so when preparing to drink: (O:) or, as is said in the L, from ma$orabapN as syn. with gurofapN : (TA:) you say, Ai$oraA^ab~a lahu , (S, A,) or A_ilayohi , (K,) or both; (TA;) [the former of which may be rendered He raised his head at it, or he stretched forth his neck at it to look; or, as also the latter, he stretched forth his neck to look at it; ] namely, a thing: (S:) or A$rA^b~ originally means he stretched forth his neck in preparing to drink water: and then, in consequence of frequency of usage, he raised his head, and stretched forth his neck, in looking; and hence is trans. by means of A_ilaY : (Har p. 152:) or he raised, or exalted, himself. (K, * TA.) ya$oray^ib~uwna liSawotihi , occurring in a trad., means (tropical:) They will raise their heads at his voice to look at him. (TA.) And Ai$oraA^ab~a Aln~ifaAqu waA@rotad~ati AlEarabu , in another trad., means (tropical:) Hypocrisy exalted itself [ and the Arabs apostatized, or revolted from their religion ]. (TA.)

definition: A single act of drinking.
sourceDefinition: A single act of drinking. (S.) ― -b2- And A single draught, or the quantity that is drunk at once, of water. (S.) It is said in a prov., niEoma miEolaqu Al$~arobapi h`*aA [ Excellent, or most excellent, is the traveller's drinking-cup, or bowl, that will hold a single draught, namely, this! ]: the miEolaq is said by As to be a drinking-cup or bowl which the rider upon a camel suspends [to his saddle]: (Meyd:) it is said in describing a camel: (TA:) and it means that, to the place of alighting to which he desires to go, he is content with a single draught, not wanting another: (Meyd, TA:) the prov. is applied to him who, in his affairs, is content with his own opinion, not wanting that of another person. (Meyd.) $arobapu A^abiY Aljahomi [ The draught of Abu-l-Jahm ] is said of a thing that is sweet, or pleasant, but in its result unwholesome: (MF, TA:) Abu-l-Jahm was a frequent visiter of the Khaleefeh El-Mansoor El-'Abbásee, who, finding him troublesome, ordered that a poisoned draught should be given to him, in his presence: which having been done, Abu-l-Jahm, pained by the draught, rose to depart; and being asked by the Khaleefeh whither he was going, he answered, Whither thou hast sent me, O Prince of the Faithful. (MF.) ― -b3- In the Mo'allakah of Tarafeh, it is applied to A draught of wine. (EM p. 87.) ― -b4- [In the conventional language of the physicians, it is a term applied to A dose of medicine, such as is drunk and also such as is eaten. ] -A2- Also A palm-tree that grows from the date stone: (K:) pl. $arabaAtN . (TA. [It seems to be there added that $araAy^ibu and $araAbiybu are also its pls.: the former may be like DaraAy^iru pl. of Dar~apN : the latter is app. a mistranscription, and should perhaps be $araAy^iybu , for $araAy^ibu ; like maHaAmiyru for maHaAmiru , &c.])

definition: [The act, or habit, of ] much drinking.
sourceDefinition: [The act, or habit, of ] much drinking. (K.) One says, A_in~ahu la*Fw $arabapK , meaning Verily he is one who drinks much. (AA, AHn, TA.) -A2- It is also allowable as a pl. of $aAribN [q. v.]. (Msb.) -A3- Also A small trough, (S, K, TA,) made, (S,) or dug, (TA,) around a palm-tree, (S, K, TA,) and around any other kind of tree, and filled with water, (TA,) holding enough to irrigate it fully, (K, TA,) so that it is plentifully irrigated thereby: (S, TA:) pl. ↓ $arabN [or rather this is a coll. gen. n., of which the former is the n. un.,] and [the pl. properly so termed is] $arabaAtN . (S.) ― -b2- And i. q. kurodu daborapK , (K, TA,) which is syn. with masoqaApN : (TA:) [from a comparison of the explanations of all of these words, it seems to mean A channel of water for the irrigation of a plot, or tract, of sown land: or, if the explanation msqAp , in the TA, be conjectural, the meaning may be a portion of such land, having a raised border to retain the water admitted upon it: ] pl. $arabaAtN and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ $arabN [as above]. (TA.) -A4- Also Thirst. (Lh, T, O, K.) One says, lamo tazalo bihi $arabapN Alyawoma He has not ceased to have thirst to-day. (Lh, TA.) And jaA='ati AlA_ibilu wabihaA $arabapN The camels came thirsty. (T, O.) And TaEaAmN *uw $arabapK Food wherewith one has not sufficient water to satisfy thirst. (O, TA.) Accord. to the L, $arabapN signifies The thirst of cattle after the being satisfied with fresh pasture; because this invites to drink. (TA.) ― -b2- And Vehemence of heat. (K.) One says, yawomN *uw $arabapK A day of vehement heat, in which is drunk more water than at other times. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ $ariybN are syn. with $araAbN , q. v.: or both signify Water inferior to the Ea*ob [or sweet ]: (K:) or [ brackish water; i. e.] water between the salt and the sweet: (AO, S:) or water drinkable, or fit to be drunk, but in which is disagreeableness: (Msb:) or the former signifies water that has some degree of sweetness, and is sometimes drunk by men notwithstanding what is in it; and ↓ the latter, water inferior to what is sweet, and not drunk by men save in cases of necessity, but sometimes drunk by cattle: (IKtt, TA:) or ↓ the latter, the sweet: and the former is said to signify water that is drunk: (TA:) or ↓ the latter, water that has no sweetness in it, but is sometimes drunk by men notwithstanding what is in it; and the former, water inferior to this in sweetness, and not drunk by men save in cases of necessity: (AZ, T, M, TA:) or, accord. to Lth, ↓ $ariybN and ↓ $ir~iybN signify water in which are bitterness and saltness, but not abstained from as drink: and maA='N $aruwbN and TaEiymN are syn.: and ↓ maA='N mi$orabN is syn. with $aruwbN : this last word is used alike as masc. and fem. and sing. and pl. definition: Drinking, or a drinker: pl.
sourceDefinition: Drinking, or a drinker: pl. $aAribuwna (Msb) and ↓ $arobN , like as SaHobN is of SaAHibN , (S, Msb,) or, accord. to ISd, (TA,) $arobN , which signifies people drinking, (K, TA,) and assembling for drinking, is a quasi.-pl. n. of $aAribN , being like rakobN and rajolN ; and $uruwbN , which is said by IAar [and in the S] to be pl. of $arobN , is pl. of $aAribN , like as $uhuwdN is of $aAhidN ; (TA;) $arabapN also is allowable as a pl. of $aAribN , like as kafarapN is pl. of kaAfirN ; (Msb;) and A^a$orubN is pl. of $arobN , or it may be an anomalous pl. of $aAribN : (MF:) the pl. $uruwb occurs in the saying of El-Aashà, huwa AlwaAhibu AlmusomiEaAti Al$~uruw ba bayona AlHariyri wabayona Alkatano [ He is the giver of female singers to the drinkers, some clad in silk and some in linen ]. (S.) ― -b2- See also $ir~iybN . ― -b3- [Hence, The mustache; i. e.] the defluent hair over the mouth; (Msb;) or so $awaAribu , (Lh, A, K,) which is the pl., (Lh, S, Msb,) as though the sing, applied to every distinct part: (Lh:) the two [halves] are called $aAribaAni : (S, TA:) or, as some say, only the sing. is used, and the dual is a mistake: (TA:) accord. to AHát (Msb, TA) and AAF, (TA,) the dual is is scarcely ever, or never, used; but accord. to AO, the Kilábees say $aAribaAni , with regard to the two extremities: (Msb, TA:) and the pl., (A, K,) or, accord. to the T &c., the dual, (TA,) signifies the long portions [ of the hair ] on the two sides of the sabalap [q. v.]: (T, A, K, TA:) or (K, TA) $aAribN signifies the sabalap altogether, (A, K, TA,) as some say; but this is not correct. (TA.) One says, Tar~a $aAribu AlgulaAmi [ The mustache of the boy, or young man, grew forth ]. (S.) ― -b4- And hence, as being likened to the two long portions of hair on each side of the sabalap , the $aAribaAni of the sword, (T, TA,) i. e. (tropical:) Two long projections ( A^anofaAni TawiylaAni ) at the lower part of the hilt, (A, * K, TA,) [ extending from the guard, ] one on one side and the other on the other side of the blade, (T, * TA,) the gaA$iyap [or leathern covering of the scabbard ] being beneath them: so says ISh. (TA.) ― -b5- Al$~awaAribu also signifies (tropical:) The Euruwq [or ducts ] of the Huloquwm [or windpipe ]: (A:) or certain ducts ( Euruwq ) in the Haloq [i. e. fauces or throat ], (K, TA,) that imbibe the water [or saliva? ], being the channels thereof: (TA:) and, (K,) or, as some say, (TA,) the channels of the water [or saliva? ] (S, K, TA) in the Haloq [i. e. fauces or throat ] (S) or in the neck: (K, TA:) or certain ducts ( Euruwq ) adhering to the windpipe, and the lower parts thereof to the lungs: so says IDrd: or rather, some say, the hinder part thereof [ adhering ] to the watiyn [or aorta ], having tubes from which the voice issues, and in which choking takes place, and whence the saliva issues: and those of the horse are said to be [ certain ducts ] by the side of the A^awodaAj [or external jugular veins ], where the veterinary surgeon draws blood by cutting the AwdAj : the sing. seems by implication to be $aAribN . (TA.) Hence the phrase HimaArN Saxibu Al$~awaAribi (assumed tropical:) An ass that brays vehemently. (S, TA.) And Saxibu Al$~awaAribi (tropical:) [A man] having a disagreeable voice: thus likened to an ass. (A, TA.) ― -b6- Accord. to IAar, Al$~awaAribu signifies [also] majaAriY AlmaA='i fiY AlEayoni , which AM supposes to mean The channels of water in the spring, or source; not in the eye. (L, TA.) ― -b7- sunobulN $aAribu qamoHK means (tropical:) Ears of corn becoming, or being, pervaded by the farina: (A, TA:) or, in which the grain has hardened, and nearly come to maturity. (TA.) -A2- Also (assumed tropical:) Weakness, or feebleness, in any animal: (K, * TA:) or a strain ( Eiroq ) thereof; as in the saying, niEoma AlbaEiyru h`*aA lawolaA A^an~a fiyhi $aAriba xawarK (assumed tropical:) [ Excellent, or most excellent, were the camel, this one, were there not in him a strain of weakness or feebleness ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ The sun; ] the body of the solar light, that runs its course in the firmament: (Lth, * TA:) it is fem.: (S, * Msb, K:) and has neither dual nor pl.: (Msb:) or it has a pl., [though this is not used in a pl. sense,] namely, $umuwsN , (S, K,) as though they called every part of it a $ms , like as they said mafaAriqu for maforiqN . (S.) When it is made determinate without the article Al , [as] in the name Eabodu $amosa , meaning The Servant of the Sun, (Msb, K,) i. e., of this luminous object, (Msb,) the $ms of heaven, because they used to worship it, (K,) it is imperfectly decl., (Aboo- 'Alee, Msb, K,) because it is determinate and of the fem. gender, (Aboo-'Alee, K,) or because it is a proper name and of the fem. gender and altered from Al$~amos : (Msb:) and a poet says, kal~aA wa$amosa lanaxoDiban~ahumu damFA [ Nay verily, by the sun, we will assuredly dye them with blood ], making $ms imperfectly decl. because he means the art. Al to be understood: (IAar, TA:) but some say that in the former instance, (Msb, TA,) and in the latter, (TA,) the word in question has a different signification, which will be shown below: (Msb, TA:) and Sb says that none of the Arabs made $ms determinate without the art. Al , except in the proper name mentioned above, in which all of them made it so. (TA.) The dim. is ↓ $umayosapN . (S, TA.) ― -b2- [Also The sun, or sunshine. ] You say, qaEada fiY Al$~amosi [ He sat in the sun, or sunshine ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, (K, TA,) or $amosN , (Msb,) A certain ancient idol. (Msb, K.) Accord. to Ibn-El-Kelbee, it is this that is meant by the proper name mentioned above; and if so, it is perfectly decl.: (Msb:) and some say that it is this also that is meant in the words of the poet cited above, and that he makes the word imperfectly decl. because he uses it as a proper name of the image ( AlS~uwrap ). (TA.) -A2- $amosN also signifies A kind of necklace or collar: (S, K:) or a pendant, or suspended ornament, ( miEolaAq ,) of the necklace or collar upon the neck: or the collar of a dog: (TA:) or a kind of women's ornament: of the masc. gender: (Lh, TA:) pl. $umuwsN . (TA.) ― -b2- And A kind of comb, (K,) with which women in the first age used to comb themselves; (TA;) as also ↓ $amosapN . (IDrd, TA.) -A3- yawomN $amosN : see $aAmisN .

definition: $w~lt , said of a she-camel, (S, O, K,) She became such as is termed $aAy^ilap : (S, O, TA: [in one of my copies of the S, SaAra $awolFA is erroneously put for SaArato $aAy^ilapF :]) or her supplies of milk dried up;
sourceDefinition: $w~lt , said of a she-camel, (S, O, K,) She became such as is termed $aAy^ilap : (S, O, TA: [in one of my copies of the S, SaAra $awolFA is erroneously put for SaArato $aAy^ilapF :]) or her supplies of milk dried up; ( jaf~ato A^alobaAnuhaA ; K, TA; [but perhaps the right reading is xaf~ato , meaning became scanty; for SM adds,]) and became little in quantity. (TA.) And $w~lt AlA_ibilu The camels became in such a state that their bellies [ were drawn up as though they ] reached their backs: (K, TA:) or became such as to have [ only ] a $awol [or small quantity remaining ] of milk: like as one says, (O, TA,) $w~lt AlmazaAdapu The mzAdp [or leathern water-bag ] had little water remaining in it: (O, K, TA:) one should not say $aAlat . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, app.,] ta$owiylN of the *akar signifies Its being in a relaxed state on the occasion of mujaAmaEap . (O, K.) And $w~l said of a horse means, like raf~aDa , He put forth his veretrum without being vigorously lustful. (TA in art. rfD .) ― -b3- $w~l said of a garob [or large bucket], Its water became little in quantity. (O, K.) Said of a she-camel's milk, It became deficient: (K, TA:) and it became withdrawn. (TA.) And said of water, It became little in quantity. (K.) ― -b4- In the following saying, (S, TA,) of Abu-n-Nejm, (TA,) Hat~aY A_i*aA maA AlEi$oru EanohaA $aw~alaA the poet means, *ahaba and taSar~ama [i. e. Until, when the coming to water on the tenth day after the next preceding period of abstinence ceased from her or them... referring to a camel or to camels]. (S, TA.) ― -b5- $w~l fiY AlmazaAdapi He left somewhat remaining ( A^aboqaY $awolFA ) of water in the mzAdp [or leathern water-bag ]. (K, * TA.)

(TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Al$~awolapu (assumed tropical:) Two bright stars, near together, [ λ and ν ,] (S, O,) in the end of the tail of Scorpio, (Kzw,) which are one of the Mansions of the Moon, (S, O, Kzw,) namely, the Nineteenth Mansion; (Kzw;) also called Humapu AlEaqorabi . (S, O.) [See manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl .] ― -b3- And $awolapu is a proper name for The scorpion; (O, TA;) [and] so ↓ $aw~aAlapu . (K, TA.) -A2- Also A foolish, or stupid, woman. (IAar, O, K.) $awolapu was the name of A certain foolish female slave, belonging to [the tribe of] 'Adwán, and she used to give advice to her masters, and it resulted in evil to them; whence the saying, A^anota $awolapu Aln~aASiHapu [ Thou art Showleh the giver of advice ]. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- Also the name of The mare of Zeyd-el-Fawáris Ed-Dabbee. (O, K.)

definition: A certain plant, (AHn, O, K,) mentioned, but not described, by As;

definition: The tail of the scorpion.
sourceDefinition: The tail of the scorpion. (TA. [So called because often raised.]) ― -b2- Also, (S, O, Msb, K,) and sometimes it is called Al$~aw~aAlu , (Msb,) The month of the festival of the breaking of the fast; (Msb, K; *) the month next after ramaDaAn ; (TA;) the first of the months of the pilgrimage; (S, O;) [ the tenth month of the lunar year: ] as some assert, (IDrd, O,) so called because [when first thus named] it coincided with the season when the she-camels [being seven or eight months gone with young] raised their tails: (IDrd, O, Msb, TA:) [for the camels generally couple in winter:] or because of their milk becoming then withdrawn; such being the case with the camels in the time of vehement heat and of the coming to an end of the juicy fresh herbage: [see a table of the months voce zamanN :] the Arabs used to regard the making of marriage-contracts in this month as of evil omen; and to say that the woman [then] married would resist him who married her, like as the she-camel resists the stallion and raises her tail; but the Prophet abolished their thus auguring, and he married 'Áïsheh in this month: (TA:) the pl. is $aw~aAlaAtN and $awaAwiylu (S, Msb, K) and $awaAwilu , this last formed by rejecting the augmentative letter [in the second]. (TA.)

(K.)

definition: A she-camel raising her tail, (S, O, Msb, K,) having conceived, (Msb,) or by reason of having conceived, and having no milk whatever: (S, O, K:) or a she-camel that has conceived, and raises her tail...
sourceDefinition: A she-camel raising her tail, (S, O, Msb, K,) having conceived, (Msb,) or by reason of having conceived, and having no milk whatever: (S, O, K:) or a she-camel that has conceived, and raises her tail to the stallion as a sign of her having conceived, raising her head therewith, and elevating her nose: (Az, TA:) the word is without p because it is an epithet of peculiar application [to a female]: (Msb:) or it is without p anomalously; for the male also raises his tail: (ISd, TA:) the pl. is $uw~alN (Az, S, O, Msb, K) and $uy~alN and $iy~alN and $uw~aAlN . (K.) Also, with p , applied to a mare, as meaning Raising the tail. (TA.) ― -b2- And $aAy^ilapN , which is anomalously with p because it is an epithet denoting an attribute not shared with the female by the male, (ISd, TA,) A she-camel that has passed seven months, (S, O, K,) or eight, (S, O,) since the period of her bringing forth, (S, O, K,) or of her becoming pregnant, (K,) and whose milk has dried up, ( jaf~a labanuhaA , K, and so in a copy of the S,) or whose milk has become scanty, ( xaf~a labanuhaA , O, and so in another copy of the S,) and her udder drawn up, (S, O,) there remaining in her udder no more than a $awol , a third of the quantity of the contents thereof when her bringing forth was recent: (TA:) she-camels in this case are termed ↓ $awolN , (S, O, K,) an anomalous pl., (K,) [or rather a quasi-pl. n.,] expl. by some as applied to she-camels whose milk has become deficient, which is the case when their young are weaned at the period of the [auroral] rising of suhayol [or Canopus, a period which commenced, in Central Arabia, about the beginning of the era of the Flight, on the 4th of August, O. S.], and they cease not to be thus termed until the stallion is sent among them; (TA;) the pl. pl. [or pl. of $awolN ] is A^a$owaAlN ; (K;) and $awaAy^ilu is a pl. of $aAy^ilapN meaning [as expl. above, or] a she-camel whose milk has become withdrawn. (TA.) ― -b3- $aAy^ilN is also applied to Anything that is raised, or drawn up, or withdrawn. (TA.)

definition: (A, Msb, K) and ↓ Sax~aAbN (S, A, Msb, K) and ↓ SaxobaAnu (S, Msb, K) and ↓ SaxuwbN (K) and ↓ SaAxibN (A, Msb) are epithets from Saxiba ;
sourceDefinition: (A, Msb, K) and ↓ Sax~aAbN (S, A, Msb, K) and ↓ SaxobaAnu (S, Msb, K) and ↓ SaxuwbN (K) and ↓ SaAxibN (A, Msb) are epithets from Saxiba ; (S, A, Msb, K;) all except the last signifying One who clamours, or raises confused cries or shouts or noises, vehemently, or much; (TA;) [the last having a similar, but not intensive, signification, i. e. clamouring, &c.:] and the first, though masc., is applied by the poet Usámeh ElHudhalee to a female singer considered as a person ( $axoS [and meaning in this instance loud of voice ]); for an epithet of the measure faEilN applied to a woman ( AimoraA^apN ) is not known in the language: (L, TA:) the [proper] fem. epithet is SaxibapN and ↓ Sax~aAbapN (K) and ↓ SaxobaY (Msb) and ↓ SaxuwbN (K, TA, in the CK [erroneously] SaxuwbapN ) and ↓ Suxub~apN : (K:) the pl. of SaxobaAnu is ↓ SuxobaAnN ; (Kr, K;) [and the pl. of SaxuwbN is ↓ SuxubN , like SuburN pl. of SabuwrN :] the hypocrites are described in a trad. as SuxubN biAln~ahaAri xu$ubN biAll~ayoli [expl. voce xa$abN ], meaning clamorous and contentious. sourceDefinition: , (L, K,) an inf. n. of Saraxa , (S,) signifies The calling or calling out, or crying or crying out, vehemently; [or screaming; ] (L, K;) on an occasion of fright, or alarm, or of some affliction, or evil accident: (L:) one says, Saraxa , inf. n. SaroxapN ; and ↓ ASTrx ; [ He called or called out, &c.;] both meaning the same. (S.) And SuraAxN is also an inf. n. of Saraxa , (A, Mgh, Msb,) and signifies The raising the voice, calling or calling out, crying or crying out: (S, A, L, K:) or doing so vehemently: (L, K:) and the calling, or crying, for aid, or succour; (A;) which last meaning is said to be tropical, but conventionally regarded as proper; (MF;) as also SariyxN , (S, TA,) which is likewise an inf. n. of Saraxa : (A, Mgh:) one says, Saraxa , aor. (TK.) kaAnato kaSaroxapi AlHubolaY [ It was like the vehement crying-out, or the screaming, of the pregnant woman ] is a prov., said of a thing that comes upon one suddenly, when he is not aware. (T.)

definition: He called, or cried, to him for aid, or succour.
sourceDefinition: He called, or cried, to him for aid, or succour. (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb.) ― -b2- And He incited him, urged him, or induced him, to call or call out, to cry or cry out, [app. for aid, or succour, ] or to do so vehemently. (L, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence,] AusotuSorixa AlA_inosaAnu There came to the man a voice, or cry, informing him of an event on account of which his aid was invoked, or announcing to him a death. (IAth, TA.) AisotiSoraAxu AlHaY~i means The tribe's being invoked for aid to perform what is requisite for the dead: and hence the trad. of Ibn-'Omar, faA@sotuSorixa EalaY A@moraA^atihi , not biA@moraA^atihi , meaning, And he was called to aid in furnishing for the grave, and burying, the corpse of his wife: or it may mean, was informed that his wife was at the point of death. (Mgh.) -A2- See also 1, in two places; and 6: ― -b2- and see 4.

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. yaSoliyhi , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. SaloYN , (S, M, K,) He roasted, broiled, or fried, it, namely, flesh-meat, (S, M, Msb, K,) &c.; (S;) and SalaAhu fiY Aln~aAri and EalaY Aln~aAri signify the same; and also he burned it. (TA.) And (so in the M, but in the K “ or ”) SalaAhu (M, K) fiY Aln~aAri (M) He threw it into the fire to be burned; as also ↓ ASlAhu ; and ↓ Sl~Ahu , (M, K,) inf. n. taSoliyapN ; (TA;) namely, flesh-meat. (M, K. [But see the next sentence.]) And SalaAhu Aln~aAra and fiY Aln~aAri and EalaY Aln~aAri , (M, K,) inf. n. SaloYN and SuliY~N and SiliY~N ; (M;) and Aln~aAra ↓ ASlAhu , and Aln~aAra ↓ Sl~Ahu ; He made him to enter into the fire, and to remain, stay, dwell, or abide, therein: (M, K:) and fulaAnN Aln~aAra ↓ Sul~iYa [ Such as one was made to enter into the fire, &c.]: (M:) [or] you say, Salayotu Alr~ajula naArFA , meaning I made the man to enter fire and to be burned: and ↓ A^aSolayotuhu , with A , when you mean I threw him, or cast him, into the fire, as though intending burning [ him ]; as also ↓ Sal~ayotuhu , inf. n. taSoliyapN . (S.) ― -b2- And Salayotu fulaAnFA , (T, TA,) or lifulaAnK , (S, TA,) (tropical:) I laboured in a case, or an affair, desiring to calumniate, or slander, such a one therein, and to cause him to fall into destruction: (T, S, TA:) or Salayotuhu and Salayotu lahu both signify I calumniated, or slandered, him, and caused him to fall into destruction, (M, TA,) in consequence thereof: (M:) or, accord. to the K, SalaY fulaAnFA , of which the inf. n. is SaloYN , signifies he soothed, coaxed, wheedled, or cajoled, such a one: or deceived, deluded, beguiled, circumvented, or outwitted, him: which meanings are not in any of the three lexicons above mentioned: accord. to the A, Salayotu bifulaAnK [probably a mistranscription for lifulaAnK ] means (tropical:) I framed a stratagem, or plot, to cause such a one to fall; there said to be tropical. (TA.) ― -b3- SalaY yadahu biAln~aAri [said in the TA to be a mistake]: see 2. -A2- SaliYa Aln~aAra , (S, M, Msb, K,) and biAln~aAri , (M, Msb, K,) aor. yaSolaY , (S, Msb, * K, *) inf. n. SalFY , (Msb,) or SuliY~N , (S, K, [ SaloyFA in the CK being a mistranscription for Suliy~FA ,]) or both, (M,) and SiliY~N and SilaA='N , (M, K,) and accord. to the K SalaA='N , but this is a mistake for SalFY , (TA,) He was, or became, burned [ by the fire ]: (S:) or he endured, or suffered, the heat of the fire; as also Aln~aAra ↓ tSl~Y : (M, K:) or he felt the heat of the fire: (Msb:) and one says ↓ tSl~Y Har~a Aln~aAri and ↓ ASTlAhu [in this last sense or in the sense next preceding]: (Ham p. 792:) and SaliYa Aln~aAra he entered into the fire: (TA in art. blh : see an ex. voce baloha :) or, accord. to Er-Rághib, SaliYa biAln~aAri means he was tried ( buliYa ) by fire, or by the fire; and so bika*aA (assumed tropical:) [ by such a thing, as though by fire ]. (TA.) [In the Kur, in which are many exs. of it, (iv. 11, xiv. 34, xvii. 19, &c.,) it is always trans. by itself, without bi .] And SaliYa biAlA^amori , (S, M, *) and biAlHarobi ; (S;) and AlA^amora ↓ tSl~Y , and AlHaroba ; (M;) He endured, or suffered, the heat, and severity, or vehemence, of the affair, or case, and of the war, or fight: (S, M:) Aboo-Zubeyd says, Har~a Harobihimu ↓ faqado taSal~ayotu Almaqoruwru mino qarasi ↓ kamaA taSal~aY [ And I have suffered the heat and vehemence of their war, like as he who is affected with cold suffers in consequence of coldest and most abundant hoar-frost ]. (M.) -A3- [It is said that] SaliYa Alr~ajulu signifies also lazima [i. e. The man kept to, or clave to, a thing]; and so ↓ ASTlY : whence Zj holds SalaApN [expl. in art. Slw ] to be derived; because it is a keeping, or cleaving, to that which God has appointed: and hence also, [it is said,] fiY Aln~aAri ↓ mano yuSal~aY , i. e. ylzm [app. yulozamu , meaning mano yulozamu Aln~aAra He who is made to keep, or cleave, to the fire; nearly agreeing with Sal~aAhu Aln~aAra as expl. above from the M and K]. (TA.) -A4- And Salayotu AlZ~ahora means I struck, or beat, that part of the back which is called SalFA : or I hit that part: but this is extr.; for by rule it should be Salawotuhu , like as Hudheyl say. (M. [See 1 in art. Slw .])

definition: He warmed himself (M, K) biAln~aAri [ by means of the fire ]: (M:) one says, AiSoTalayotu biAln~aAri and bihaA ↓ taSal~ayotu [app.
sourceDefinition: He warmed himself (M, K) biAln~aAri [ by means of the fire ]: (M:) one says, AiSoTalayotu biAln~aAri and bihaA ↓ taSal~ayotu [app. meaning I warmed myself by means of the fire ]: (S:) or ASTlY Aln~aAra and biAln~aAri mean he became warm by means of the fire: and biAln~aAri ↓ tSl~Y , he became burnt by the fire. (MA.) Hence, in the Kur [xxvii. 7 and xxviii. 29], laEal~akumo taSoTaluwna [ May-be ye will warm yourselves ]: (TA:) in relation to which it is said that the time was winter, and therefore AlAiSoTilaA=' was needed. (M, TA.) ― -b2- It is also said of the chameleon, as meaning He repaired to the sun. sourceDefinition: , aor. , (K,) inf. n. Dab~N , (S, K,) He, or it, clave to the ground: (S, * K:) [like DabaA^a :] this is the primary signification. (S.) ― -b2- And, aor. and inf. n. as above, It flowed: (K, TA:) like baD~a : or it flowed gently, or scantily; as blood when it does not drop, or issue in drops, so as to require the repetition of the ablution for prayer: (TA:) or it is only said of blood and of saliva: (K:) or, aor. as above, inf. n. DabiybN , said of water and of blood, it flowed. (S.) And Dab~ato $afatuhu , aor. as above, inf. n. Dab~N and DubuwbN , His lip flowed with blood, from a tumour &c. (TA. [See also another meaning in what follows.]) And Dab~ato livatuhu damFA His gum flowed with blood: (S:) or Db~t biAld~ami : and in like manner, yaduhu [ his hand or arm ]: (A:) and tarakotu livataha taDiyb~u mina Ald~ami , inf. n. DabiybN , I left his gum flowing with blood. (TA.) Dab~atE livatuhu , aor. as above, inf. n. Dab~N , means His gum watered, or flowed with saliva. (TA.) And one says, jaA='a fulaAnN taDib~u livaAtuhu (tropical:) [ Such a one came with his gums watering ] (S, A *) lika*aA waka*aA [ for such and such things ], (A,) when the person spoken of is vehemently eager, or greedy, for a thing, (S, A,) or when he is affected with very inordinate desire to eat, or with vehement lust, or carnal desire, or with vehement eagerness, or greediness, for the accomplishment of an object of want. (L, TA.) Bishr Ibn-Abee-Kházim says, wabaniY tamiymK qado laqiynaA minohumu xayolFA taDiyb~u livaAtuhaA lilomagonami (assumed tropical:) [ And the sons of Temeem, we have found, of them, horsemen whose gums water for spoil ]: in which taDib~u is said by AO to be formed by transposition from tabiD~u . (S.) [See another ex. in a verse cited voce A^azomalN .] Another poet says, A^abayonaA A^abayonaA A^ano taDib~a livaAtukumo EalaY xur~adK mivoli AlZ~ibaA='i wajaAmili (assumed tropical:) [ We disallow, we disallow, that your gums should water for virgins, or bashful virgins, like gazelles, and for camels ]. (TA.) One says also, Dab~a famuhu , aor. as above, inf. n. Dab~N , meaning His mouth watered, or flowed with saliva: (TA:) and yaDib~u fuwhu (tropical:) [ His mouth waters ] is said of him who is vehemently eager, or greedy, for a thing. (A, TA.) ― -b3- Dab~ati Ald~aAb~apu , aor. as above, inf. n. DubuwbN , means The beast staled while running. (TA.) -A2- See also 4, in five places. -A3- Dab~a said of a boy, or male child, He became a youth, or young man; he attained to the state termed $abaAb . (TA.) -A4- Dab~ati Al$~afapu , aor. as above, (Msb, K,) inf. n. Dab~N and DubuwbN , (K,) The lip became affected with the disease termed Dab~ . (Msb, K. [See also another meaning in what precedes.]) -A5- Dab~a , (S, K,) sec. pers. Dabibota , (TA,) aor. , inf. n. DababN , said of a camel, He became affected with the disease termed Dab~ (S, K) in his firosin [i. e. in his foot, or the extremity of his foot ]. (S.) -A6- Dabiba Albaladu , (ISk, S,) or Dabibati AlA^aroDu , aor. ; and Dabubat ; (K;) [instances of reduplicative verbs preserving their original forms;] and ↓ A^aDab~a , (S,) or A^aDab~at ; (Msb, K;) The country, or land, abounded with [ the lizards called ] DibaAb , pl. of Dab~ . (S, Msb, K.) -A7- Dab~a Aln~aAqapa , aor. , (S, O,) inf. n. Dab~N , (O, K,) He milked the camel with five fingers [i. e. with his thumb and four fingers together ]: (S, O:) or with the whole hand: (K: or this mode of milking is termed Daf~N : TA:) or by putting his thumb upon the teat and turning the fingers over the thumb and the teat together: (Fr, S, O, K: this is done when the teat is long: when it is of middling length, the mode termed bazomN is adopted, with the joint of the fore finger and the extremity of the thumb: and when it is short, the mode termed faTorN , with the extremity of the fore finger and the thumb: TA:) or by taking the two teats together in the hand: (K: [or this mode of milking is termed Daf~N :] and the milking with a hard squeezing is termed ↓ Dab~apN : TA:) or by contracting the hand upon the udder, and putting the thumb in, or upon, ( fiY ,) the middle of the palm. (L, TA.) -A8- [ Dab~a and ↓ Db~b , each probably followed by EalaY , seem to signify sometimes It covered a thing, and became intermixed with it: the inf. ns. AlDbb (which I think to be a mistranscription for AlD~ab~u ) and AltDbyb are expl. in the TA as signifying “ the covering a thing, and the entering of one part, or portion, of it into another: ” see two explanations of each of these verbs, followed by EalaY , voce A^aDab~a .]

sourceDefinition: He kept, or clave, to a thing, and did not quit it: (TA:) and ADb~ fulaAnFA He kept, or clave, to such a one, and did not quit him: (K:) and ADb~ Ealayohi He retained him, detained him, or held him in custody: (AZ, K, TA:) and ADb~ maA fiY yadayohi He grasped, or kept hold of, that which was in his hands; like A^aDobaA^a and A^aDobaY . (TA in art. DbA^ .) And the first of these phrases, (TA,) inf. n. A_iDobaAbN ; (K, TA;) as also ↓ Dab~a , [aor. ,] (TA,) inf. n. Dab~N ; (K, TA;) and ↓ Db~b , (TA,) inf. n. taDobiybN ; (K, TA;) signifies AiHotawaY Ealayohi [i. e. He grasped it; got, or gained, possession of it; took it, got it, or held it, within his grasp, or in his possession: or it comprised, comprehended, or contained, it ]: (K, TA:) and EalaY $aYo'K ↓ Dab~ , inf. n. Dab~N , He took, seized, or grasped, a thing with the hand: (TA; but only the inf. n. in this case is there mentioned:) and EalaY $aYo'K ↓ Db~b , inf. n. taDobiybN , He took, seized, or grasped, a thing violently, or firmly, lest it should escape from his hand. (ISh, O, TA. [See also 1, last sentence.]) ― -b2- [It is said that] ADb~ Ealayohi also signifies He was at the point of getting possession of it, namely, a thing (O, K) that he sought, or desired. (K.) [But it seems from a passage in the TA, in which is an evident mistranscription, that this is a mistake, originated by Lth, for A^aDobaY .] -A2- ADb~ Als~iqaA='u The skin shed, or poured forth, its water, from a seam, or suture, ( xurozap ,) therein, (K, TA,) or from a cut. (TA.) [And ADb~ app. signifies He had a bleeding of the gums: for] mA zAl mDb~FA [app. ↓ muSib~FA ] occurs in a trad. said of one whose gums bled [incessantly] when he spoke. definition: [ A species of lizard;
sourceDefinition: [ A species of lizard; termed lacerta caudiverbera, from its habit of striking with its tail; (see jara$a ;) Forskål (Descr. Animalium, p. 13,) terms it lacerta Aegyptia; referring to Hasselquist, p. 302; and adds the following description: “ femora teretia sine verrucis: cauda verticillata non longa: squamæ patentes, subconicæ mucronatæ: corpus nudum, rugosum: ”] a certain reptile, or small creeping thing, (S, TA,) of those termed Ha$araAt , (TA,) well known; (K, TA;) resembling the waral [q. v., but not so long ]: (TA:) or resembling the Hiro*awn [q. v.]; of which there are two species, one of the size of the Hr*wn , and one larger: (Msb:) accord. to 'Abd-El-Káhir, of the size of a little young crocodile; having a tail like the tail of the latter: it assumes various colours when exposed to the sun, like as does the chameleon; lives seven hundred years; drinks not water, being satisfied with the air; voids one drop of urine in every forty days; its teeth consist of one curved piece; when it has quitted its hole it knows it not; and it lays eggs, like a bird: so say IKh and Dmr and others: AM says, the waral is of a lank make, with a long tail; the latter resembling that of a serpent; and the length of some exceeds two cubits; but the tail of the Db~ is jointed, and its utmost length is a span: the Arabs deem the wrl a foul and filthy thing, and do not eat it; but they are eager to hunt and eat the Db~ : this animal has a rough tail, serrated with jags resembling vertebræ; its colour inclines to a blackish dusty hue; and when it becomes fat, its breast becomes yellow; it eats nothing but [ the locusts called ] janaAdib , and young locusts before their wings have grown ( dabFA ), and herbage, not venomous or noxious reptiles; whereas the wrl eats scorpions and serpents and chameleons and beetles: its flesh is an antidote against poisons, and women grow fat upon it: (L, TA:) it is the longest, of the animals, in retaining the remains of life: (O:) [see also muTab~ixN :] the fem. is with p : (S, O, Msb, K:) and the pl. [of pauc.] is A^aDub~N and [of mult.] DibaAbN (S, O, Mgh, Msb, K) and Dub~aAnN , (K,) which last Lh particularizes as used to denote a great number, but ISd sees no reason for this distinction, (TA,) and [quasipl. n.] ↓ maDab~apN , (O, K,) like as ma$oyaxapN is of $ayoxN , (O,) this last on the authority of As, as heard by him from more than one of the Arabs. (TA.) Hence one says rajulN xab~N Dab~N (tropical:) [ A very deceitful or mischievous, and ] an abominable, guileful, ireful man: (TA:) or a very deceitful or mischievous or wicked, and guileful man: (S:) likened to the [lizard called] Dab~ on account of his guilefulness: and in like manner, AimoraA^apN xab~apN Dab~apN . (A, TA.) And A^axodaEu mina AlD~ab~i More guileful than the Db~ : (A, TA:) a prov. (TA.) And A^aEaq~u mino Dab~K [ More undutiful to kindred than a Db~ ]; because the Db~ often eats its Husuwl [or young ones when they have just come forth from the eggs]: another prov.: (S:) A^abuw HisolK is a surname of the Db~ . (TA.) One says also A^aTowalu *amaA='F mina AlD~ab~i , another prov. [expl. in art. *mY ]. (O.) And A^aHoyaru mino Dab~K , which is likewise a prov. [expl. in art. Hyr ]. (Har p. 166.) And A^atuEolimuniY biDab~K A^anaA Hara$otuhu , another prov. [expl. in art. Hr$ ]. (TA.) And laA A^afoEaluhu Hat~aY yaHin~a AlD~ab~u fiY A_ivori AlA_ibili AlS~aAdirapi [ I will not do it until the Db~ utters a yearning cry at the heels of the camels returning from water ]: and laA A^afoEaluhu Hat~aY yarida AlD~ab~u [ I will not do it until the Db~ comes to water: i. e. I will never do it:] because the Db~ does not drink water. (S, O.) kaf~u AlD~ab~i [means The paw of the Db~ ]: to this the Arabs liken the hand of the niggard when he fails to give: (TA:) and it is also applied by way of comparison to (tropical:) a niggard himself: and to denote (tropical:) shortness and littleness. (A, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence also,] (tropical:) Rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite, (S, A, O, Msb, K, TA,) latent in the heart; (A, TA;) like the [lizard called] Db~ hiding itself in the furthest extremity of its hole: (A:) and anger, wrath, or rage: (K:) or rancour, &c., or vehement rancour, &c., and enmity: (TA:) and ↓ Dib~N signifies the same: (K:) the pl. is DibaAbN , and [app. DibabN also, for] the phrase kul~N minohumaA HaAmilu DibabK liSaAHibihi [ Each of them a bearer of latent rancours &c. towards his fellow ] occurs in a trad. (TA.) -A2- Also A certain disease in the lip, (S, O, Msb, K,) in consequence of which it flows with blood, (S, O, Msb,) or swells, and becomes hard, or dry and hard, and flows with blood. (TA.) ― -b2- And A tumour in the breast of a camel. (O, K.) ― -b3- And A tumour (S, O, K) in the xuf~ , (so in copies of the K [i. e. foot ], in the TA Anf [which is, I doubt not, a mistranscription],) or in the firosin , [which means the same, or the extremity of the foot, ] (S, O,) of the camel. (S, O, K.) ― -b4- And A disease in the elbow of a camel; (K, TA;) said to be its cutting into his skin [ by rubbing against it ]; or its being distorted, and falling against his side, so as to gall it. (TA.) ― -b5- And A chapping, or cracking, ( AinafitaAqN ,) [ in the crease ] of the armpit [of a child, or of a camel], and abundance of flesh: (S, O, TA:) El- 'Adebbes El-Kinánee gives the same explanation, and says that this is what is also termed DaAgiTN . (TA. [See 5.]) -A3- Also The TaloE [i. e. the spadix, or the spathe, ] of the palm-tree: pl. DibaAbN : (S, O:) or ↓ Dab~apN signifies, (K, TA,) and so Dab~N , (TA,) [but the latter seems to be a coll. gen. n., and the former its n. un.,] a TaloEap [meaning spathe of a palm-tree ] before it cleaves open (K, TA) from [ around ] the gariyD [or spadix ]. (TA.)

definition: A well having by the side of it another well, (As, S, O, K) and one of them becomes foul with black mud, (As, S, O,) or and one of them becomes choked up, and foul with black mud, (K,) so that its...
sourceDefinition: A well having by the side of it another well, (As, S, O, K) and one of them becomes foul with black mud, (As, S, O,) or and one of them becomes choked up, and foul with black mud, (K,) so that its water becomes stinking, and it flows into the water of the sweet well, and corrupts it, so that no one drinks of it: (As, S, O, K:) or a well that is dug by the side of another well, in consequence of which its water becomes little in quantity: or a well dug between two wells that have become choked up. (O.) -A2- And A man weak in judgment, (K, TA,) that will not be roused to action with the people: (TA:) pl. DagoTaY , (K, TA,) [like maroDaY &c.,] because it is as though it were [significant of suffering from] a disease. (TA.)

definition: A slitting in the arm-pit of a camel, (S, K,) and abundance of flesh [ in that part, pressing against the side ]: (S:) and i.
sourceDefinition: A slitting in the arm-pit of a camel, (S, K,) and abundance of flesh [ in that part, pressing against the side ]: (S:) and i. q. Dab~N : (S, K) or a thing like a bag: (TA:) a tumour in the armpit of a camel, like a bag, straitening him: (Meyd: see muEar~akN :) or skin collected together: or the base of the callous protuberance upon the breast of a camel pressing against the place of the arm-pit, and marking, or scarring, and excoriating, it. (TA.) Accord. to IDrd, baEiyrN bihi DaAgiTN means A camel whose arm-pit comes in contact with his side so as to mark it, or scar it. (TA.) -A2- (tropical:) A watcher, keeper, or guardian; a confidential superintendent; (S, K;) over a person; so called because he straitens him; (S;) or over a thing. (K.) You say, A^rosalahu DaAgiTFA EalaY fulaAnK (tropical:) He sent him as a watcher, &c., over such a one. (S, TA.) And hence what is said in the trad. of Mo'ádh, (S, L,) when his wife asked him, on his return from collecting the poor-rates in El-Yemen, where was the present which he had brought for his wife, and he answered, (L,) kaAna EalaY~a DaAgiTN [ There was over me a watcher ], (S,) or kaAna maEiY DaAgiTN [ There was with me a watcher ], meaning God, who knows the secrets of men; or he meant, by DAgT , the trust committed to him by God, which he had taken upon himself; but his wife imagined that there was with him a watcher who straitened him, and prevented his taking to please her. (L.)

definition: He (a man, TA) was, or became, slender (K, TA) in his body.
sourceDefinition: He (a man, TA) was, or became, slender (K, TA) in his body. (TA. [See also DawiYa .]) And ADwY Alqawomu The people's cattle became lean, or emaciated; like ASwY Alqwm . (IKtt, TA in art. SwY .) ― -b2- And He (a man) had offspring such as is termed DaAwiY~ born to him: and in like manner ADwt is said of a woman [as meaning she brought forth such offspring ]; (M;) or she brought forth a boy such as is so termed. (K.) AigotaribuwA walaA tuDowuwA , (S, M, Msb,) occurring in a trad., (S,) means Marry ye among women that are remote in respect of relationship, (S, M, Msb, *) and not among the relations of your paternal uncles, (S,) or and not among your near relations, lest your offspring be such as is termed DaAwiY~ : (M, Msb:) for the Arabs assert that a man's offspring from his near relation is meagre, though generous, of the nature of his people. (S, Msb.) -A2- ADwAhu He rendered it weak. (S, Msb, K *) You say, ADwY AlA^amora (tropical:) He rendered the affair weak; (S, TA;) did not render it firm, or sound; or did not perform it in a firm, or sound, manner. (S, K, TA.) ― -b2- And ADwAhu Haq~ahu (assumed tropical:) He curtailed him, or defrauded him, of his right, or due. (IAar, M, K. *) -A3- ADwAhu All~ayolu A_ilayohi The night made him to have recourse, or to betake himself, to him for protection, or refuge. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [The spleen; ] one of the intestines, (Msb,) or a piece of flesh, (K, TA,) well known, (S, O, Msb, K,) black, (or rather blackish, ] and broad, in the belly of man and of others, on the left, cleaving to the side, (TA,) or cleaving to the ribs on the left side, (Zj in his “ Khalk el-Insán, ”) and said to pertain to every ruminant except the horse, which has none: (Msb: [a strange assertion, involving a double mistake; partly originating from a saying which will be mentioned in what follows:]) it is of the masc. gender: (Lh, TA:) the pl. is TuHulN (Msb, K, TA) and A^aToHilapN and TiHaAlaAtN . (Msb. [The second and third of these pls. appear to be rare; for it is said in the TA that the first is the only pl. form: and the last is anomalous.]) One says of the horse, laA TiHaAla lahu [lit. He has no spleen ]; which is a metaphor, meaning (tropical:) he is quick, or swift, in his running; like as one says of the camel, laA maraArapa lahu [lit. “ he has no gall-bladder ”]; meaning “ he has no daring. ” (S, O.)

definition: The embroidery, or variegated or figured work, ( Ealam ,) of a garment, or piece of cloth: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K:) a Pers.
sourceDefinition: The embroidery, or variegated or figured work, ( Ealam ,) of a garment, or piece of cloth: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K:) a Pers. word, (S, A, TA,) arabicized: (S, A, Msb, K:) said to be originally tirozo , meaning, in Pers., “ even measurement: ” (TA:) [or originally TiraAzo , which has the same meaning in Pers. as the arabicized form has in Arabic:] pl. TuruzN . (Msb.) ― -b2- And A garment, or piece of cloth, woven for the Sultán: (K:) also arabicized [from the Pers. TiraAzo , meaning, a royal robe, or rich embroidered garment ]: and one also says, ↓ vawobN TiraAziY~N : (TA:) or this last is so called from a place named TiraAz . (Mgh.) ― -b3- And A place in which goodly garments or cloths are woven: (Lth, Az, A, K:) and this also is arabicized [from the Pers. TiraAzo , which has the same meaning]. (TA.) You say, Eumila h`*aA Alv~awobu fiY TiraAzi fulaAnK This garment, or piece of cloth, was made in such a one's place for weaving goodly garments or cloths. (A.) And huwa maA Eumila fiY TiraAzi A@ll~`hi (tropical:) [ It is what has been made in God's place of creation of goodly things ]: said of a beautiful face. (A, TA.) And h`*aA AlkalaAmu AlHasanu mino TiraAzi fulaAnK (tropical:) [ This beautiful language is of the elegant composition of such a one ]. (A, TA.) And huwa mina AlT~iraAzi AlA^aw~ali (tropical:) [app. He is of the first noble extraction ]. (A, TA. [See also TarozN .]) And one says of a man, when he utters a good thing of his own excogitation, h`*aA mino TiraAzihi (assumed tropical:) [ This is of his clever excogitation ]. (Sgh, TA.) And in like manner is expl. the phrase, in a trad., layosa h`*aA mino TiraAziki (assumed tropical:) This is not of thine own authorship and excogitation. (TA.) ― -b4- See also TarozN , in four places.

sourceDefinition: , (As, O, K,) [aor., app., ,] inf. n. Taf~N , (TK, [or, accord. to Freytag TufuwfN , which see in what follows,]) It (a thing) was, or became, near. (As, O, K.) You say, A^axa*otu mino mataAEiY maA xaf~a waTaf~a i. e. [ I took, of my goods, ] what [ was light, and ] was near to me. (As, O.) And Taf~a Al$~aYo'u mina Al$~aYo'i The thing was, or became, near to the thing. (O, K. *) And xu*o maA Taf~a laka , and laka ↓ A@sotaTaf~a , (S, Meyd, O, K,) and laka ↓ A^aTaf~a , (Meyd, O, TA,) Take thou what has risen to thee, and become within thy power or reach, (S, O, K, TA,) and become attainable [ to thee ], or prepared [ for thee ], (AZ, Meyd, TA,) and become near to thee: (K, TA:) or what has risen to view, and has appeared, [ to thee, ] to be taken: (TA:) [for] Taf~a , inf. n. TufuwfN , signifies it rose [app. so as to become visible ]: and it was, or became, little in quantity: the saying is a prov., relating to a man's being content with a part of that which he wants: (Meyd:) and in like manner one says, xu*o maA daf~a laka , and A@sotadaf~a : (AZ, Meyd, TA:) and Ks mentions, in relation to a man's being content with a part of that which he wants, the saying, xu*o maA Taf~a laka wadaEo laka ↓ maA A@sotaTaf~a [app. meaning, if the saying be correctly thus related, Take what is within thy power, or reach, and leave what has risen to thy view so as to invite approach ]; i. e. be content with what is within thy power. (TA.) ― -b2- Taf~ati Al$~amosu : ― -b3- and Taf~a said of a bird: see 2. ― -b4- mar~ayaTf~u [app. yaTif~N ] He passed by hastening, or going quickly.
