definition: He made defective, or deficient.
sourceDefinition: He made defective, or deficient. (TA.) You say, Tf~f , (K,) or Tf~f AlmikoyaAla , and AlmiyzaAna , (Msb,) inf. n. taTofiyfN , (S, O, Msb,) He gave short measure, and short weight; (Msb;) he made the contents of the measure to be defective, (S, O, Msb, K,) and in like manner, of the balance; (Msb;) not filling the former to its uppermost parts: (S, TA:) i. e. he did thus, cheating his companion in measure or in weight. (TA.) [Hence,] Tf~f EalaY EiyaAlihi (tropical:) He scanted his household, stinted them, or was niggardly or parsimonious towards them, in expenditure. (TA.) And Tf~f EalaY Alr~ajuli (assumed tropical:) He gave to the man less than he had taken from him. (TA.) And Tf~f AlA_inaA='a He took what was upon [or above ] the vessel [i. e. its TufaAf , or TufaAfap ]. (TA. [See also 4, last sentence.]) ― -b2- Also He made full, or complete. (TA.) [Thus it has two contr. significations.] -A2- Tf~ft Al$~amosu (tropical:) The sun drew near to setting: (TA:) [but this may be a mistranscription for ↓ Taf~at , mentioned by Golius in this sense on the authority of Z: or each may be correct: that the latter is correct, and that ↓ TafaAfN or ↓ TifaAfN is its inf. n., seems to be indicated by the fact that SM adds immediately after the explanation of the former phrase,] A^ataAnaA Einoda TfAfi Al$~amosi means (tropical:) [ He came to us ] at the sun's drawing near to setting. (TA.) ― -b2- Tf~f , said of a bird, [or ↓ Taf~a , mentioned by Freytag from Hamaker's Specim. catal. p. 49, 1. 4, of the Arabic text, or both may be correct,] The bird expanded his wings: (O, K:) so says Ibn-'Abbád. (O.) ― -b3- And Tf~f bihi Alfarasu (tropical:) The horse leaped with him. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K. [Golius has omitted this; and has assigned to Tf~f , followed by b with the person who is the object, as on the authority of the S and K, the signification of AdnA (properly A^adonaY ), meaning “ prope admovit, ” a signification belonging to A^aTaf~a , but not assigned to either of these verbs in the S nor in the K.]) Taf~afa biYa Alfarasu masojida baniY zurayoqK , in a saying of Ibn-'Omar respecting a horse-race, means (tropical:) The horse leaped with me (S, O, TA) so that he passed beyond the mosque of the Sons of Zureyk. (O, TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, O, Msb, * K) and AlA_inaA='i , (K,) and ↓ TifaAfuhu , (S, Mgh, * O, Msb, K,) and ↓ Taf~uhu , and ↓ Tafafahu , (S, Mgh, * O, K,) The quantity sufficing for the filling (S, O, Msb, K) of the [ measure called ] mk~wk (S, O, K) and of the vessel (K) to its uppermost parts: (S, O, Msb, K:) or what remains in it after the wiping off of the head thereof: (M, K: [the measure being generally in the form of a truncated cone, much smaller at the top than at the base, the quantity rising above the top is not much:]) or the jimaAm or jamaAm or jumaAm (accord. to different copies of the K [generally meaning the quantity that rises above the top after the filling ]) thereof: or the quantity sufficing for the filling thereof: (K:) or the quantity nearly sufficing for the filling thereof: (TA: [and the like explanation is given of the third word in the S &c., as will be shown by what follows:]) or the quantity that falls short of the filling thereof. definition: (S, A, O, L, Msb, K) and ↓ TunobN (L, TA) A tent-rope: (Ham p.
sourceDefinition: (S, A, O, L, Msb, K) and ↓ TunobN (L, TA) A tent-rope: (Ham p. 687:) a rope with which the xayomap and the like are tied, or made fast: (Msb:) a rope of the xibaA=' (S, O, L, TA) and of the suraAdiq [q. v.] and the like: (L, TA:) a long rope with which the srAdq of the tent is tied, or made fast; (A, K, TA;) or, as in the M, with which the tent and the srAdq are tied, or made fast, [ extending ] between the ground and the TaraAy^iq [pl. of TariyqapN , q. v.]: (TA:) and also a watid [app. meaning a tent-peg ]; thus in the K, and the like is said in the M; those who make Alwatidu in the K to be conjoined with srAdq [as though the author meant that Tnb signifies a long rope with which the srAdq of the tent, and the peg, are tied, or made fast, ] being in error: (TA: [but in my opinion, this reading which is disallowed in the TA is more probably correct than the other: in the CK, and in my MS. copy of the K, instead of waAlwatidu , we find Aw Alwtd : in a copy of the A, Aw Alwatiru , an obvious mistranscription:]) the pl. is A^aTonaAbN (S, O, Msb, K) and TinabapN ; (K;) and some of the lexicologists assert that TunubN is used as a sing. like EunuqN , and as a pl. like kutubN ; (MF, TA;) and Ibn-es-Sarráj says, in one place of his book, that it has no other pl. than A^aTonaAbN ; but in another place he says that it has this pl. accord. to those who give it a pl., thus giving to understand that there is a difference of opinion as to the plural's being allowable, and that it is used in one form as sing. and pl., which is the case: (Msb, TA:) the A^aTonaAb are the A^awaAxiY~ [pl. of A=xiy~apN ], i. e. the long ropes of the A^axobiyap [pl. of xibaA=' ]; the short ropes being called A^uSurN , sing. A_iSaArN : the former are the ropes with which the tent is tied, or made fast, between the ground and the TaraAy^iq . (TA.) As an instance of a tropical usage, (A, TA,) it is related that when El-Ash'ath contracted marriage with a woman, (A, Nh, O, Msb, L,) namely, Meleekeh Bint-Zurárah, (Nh, Msb, L,) on the terms upon which she should decide, (A, Nh, O, &c.,) and she decided upon a hundred thousand dirhems, (A, Nh, Msb, L,) rad~ahaA Eumaru A_ilaY A^aTonaAbi bayotihaA , meaning (tropical:) ' Omar reduced her to the dowry of the like of her among the women of her family; (A, Nh, O, Msb, L;) [lit., to the ropes of her tent, or to the tent-ropes of her family; ] i. e., to the ground whereon was built the condition of her family, and over which their tent-ropes extended. (Nh, L.) And another tropical usage occurs in the saying, maA bayona TunubaYi Almadiynapi A^aHowaju min~iY A_ilayohaA , (TA,) a saying ascribed to the Prophet, (O,) meaning (tropical:) What is between the two extremities, (O, TA,) and the two sides, (TA,) of the city is more in need of it than I. (O, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (tropical:) A sinew, or tendon, (S, O, K,) or ligament, (M, A,) of the body, (S, M, O, K,) that ties the joints and bones: (M:) pl. A^aTonaAbN . (M, A.) A^aTonaAbu AlA^aSaAbiEi means (tropical:) The tendons of the fingers, [or the interossei, ] on the outer side of the hand, extended above the sulaAmaY , from the wrist to the lowest parts of the fingers. (A, * and TA voce A^a$ojaEu , q. v.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) A certain tendon in the uppermost part of the chest: (K, TA:) [or,] accord. to the L, the TunubataAni [or TunubaAni ?] are two tendons [or the sterno-mastoïdes ] next the pit of the throat, that extend, or stretch, when a man turns his head aside. (TA.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) The root of a tree: (S, A, O, K:) pl. A^aTonaAbN : (A:) or this (the pl.) signifies the minor roots that branch off from the root-stock or main body of the root. (TA.) You say, taqab~aDato A^aTonaAbuhaA (tropical:) [ Its roots contracted; ] meaning it was planted. (A.) ― -b5- And A^aTonaAbu Al$~amosi (tropical:) The rays, or beams, of the sun, that extend like sinews, or tendons, at the time of its rising. (TA.) You say, mad~ati Al$~amosu A^aTonaAbahaA [and Aimotad~ato A^aTonaAbuhaA ] (tropical:) [ The sun extended its beams and its beams became extended ], meaning the sun rose. (A.) ― -b6- See also A_iTonaAbapN .

(TA.) ― -b2- EabaA^a , (AZ, S, O, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (AZ, S, O,) also signifies He made, (K,) or prepared and made, (AZ, S, O,) and mixed, perfume; (AZ, S, O, K;) and so ↓ Eb~A^ , inf. n. taEobiy^apN and taEobiYo'N ; and Eb~Y . (T, K, TA,) namely, the affair. (T, TA.) maA yaEobaA^u bikumo rab~iY , in the Kur [xxv. last verse], is said by Mujáhid to mean What will my Lord do with you? but see another explanation of this in what follows. And qado EabaA^a A@ll~`hu Eanohu God has received with approbation everything from him. (Aboo-'Adnán, TA.) ― -b5- And EabaA^a lahu He thought it, or opined it, and held it, or took to it as a tenet. (O, TA.) -A2- EabaA^a wajohuhu , aor. , His face shone: (IAar, TA:) and so EabaA , aor. yaEobuw . (K in art. Ebw .)

(S, * Mgh, * O, * K, * TA.) It is said in a trad., maA lahu taribato ↓ kaAna yaquwulu liA^aHadinaA Eani AlmaEotabapi yaminyuhu [ He used to say of one of us, from a motive of friendly anger, What aileth him? May his right hand (meaning he himself) cleave to the dust: see tariba ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And [sometimes] Eataba Ealayohi signifies [simply] He was angry with him. (Mgh, TA. *) A poet says, (S, O, TA,) namely, El-Ghatammash (O, TA) Ed-Dabbee, (TA,) A^axil~aAYa lawo gayoru AlHimaAmi A^aSaAbakumo Eatabotu wal`kino maA EalaY Ald~ahor$ maEotabu (S, O, TA; but in the O, EalaY Almawoti , and A^axil~aA='i as well as A^axil~aAYa , as in the Ham p. 406;) meaning [ O my friends, had some other event than the decreed case of death befallen you, ] I had been angry: [ but there is no being angry with fortune: ] i. e., had ye fallen in war, we had taken your blood-revenge: but one cannot revenge himself upon fortune. (TA.) ― -b3- And Eataba Ealayohi , (Msb, K, * TA, *) aor. and , inf. n. EatobN (Msb, K, TA) and Eit~iybaY [an intensive form] (K, TA) and EitobaAnN (Az, TA) and maEotabN , (Msb,) signifies also He reproved, blamed, or censured, him; (K, TA;) and so ↓ EAtbhu , (TA,) inf. n. muEaAtabapN and EitaAbN : (K, TA:) or he reproved, blamed, or censured, him, in anger, or displeasure. (Msb.) A poet says, falayosa wud~N ↓ A_i*aA *ahaba AlEitaAbu wayaboqaY Alwud~a maA baqiYa AlEitaAbu [ When reproof departs, there is no love: but love lasts as long as reproof lasts ]. (S, * O, TA.) EatobN and EitobaAnN signify Thy reproving a man for evil conduct that he has shown towards thee, and from which thou hast desired him to return to what will please thee, or make thee happy. (Az, TA. [See also the latter word below.]) -A2- maA Eatabotu baAbahu means I did not tread, or have not trodden, upon the threshold ( Eatabap ) of his door; (A, K, TA;) and so ↓ maA taEat~abotuhu . (A, TA.) ― -b2- And [hence,] Eataba , aor. and , inf. n. EatabaAnN (S, O, K) and EatobN and taEotaAbN , [this last an intensive form,] (K,) (tropical:) He (a stallion [camel], TA) limped, or halted: (K, TA:) or knocked his knees together, or had a distortion in a hind leg: or was hamstrung: (TA:) and he (a camel, S, O, or a stallion [camel], TA) walked upon three legs, (S, O, K, TA,) in consequence of his having been hamstrung, (K, TA,) or in consequence of his knees' knocking together, or of his having a distortion in a hind leg; as though he leaped: (TA:) and he (a man) leaped on one foot, or hopped, (S, O, K,) raising the other: (K:) in each of these cases, the beast or man is likened to one walking upon a series of steps, or the like, of stairs, (O, TA,) or of a mountain, or of rugged ground, (TA,) and leaping from one of these to another. (O, TA.) ― -b3- And Eataba Albaroqu , aor. and , inf. n. EatabaAnN , (assumed tropical:) The lightning flashed in continued succession. (TA.) ― -b4- And Eataba mino mawoDiEK A_ilaY mawoDiEK , aor. [and app. also], (assumed tropical:) He passed [ from place to place ], and mino qawolK A_ilaY qawolK [ from saying to saying ]. (O, TA.) ― -b5- And Etb Alqawomu fiY Als~ayori [i. e. Eataba , though Freytag assigns this meaning to Eat~aba ,] (assumed tropical:) The people, or party, turned aside in journeying, and alighted in a place not in the right, or intended, direction. (Ham p. 18. [See also 4 and 8.]) -A3- See also A^uEotiba , said of a bone.

definition: The making an Eatabap [meaning a threshold ].
sourceDefinition: The making an Eatabap [meaning a threshold ]. (K, TA.) taEotiybu AlbaAbi means The making a threshold ( Eatabap ) to the door. (TA.) ― -b2- [And The making an Eatabap (meaning a step ):] or so taEotiybu EatabapK .] You say, Eat~ibo liY EatabapF fiY h`*aA AlmawoDiEi [ Make thou for me a step in this place ] when you desire to ascend thereby to a place. (O, TA.) ― -b3- And The drawing together the Hujozap [of the drawers, or trousers, i. e. the tuck, or doubled upper border, through which passes the waist-band ], and folding it, in front: [app. meaning the turning up a portion, drawn together in front, inside the band, to prepare for some active employment:] (IAth, O, K, TA:) you say, Eat~aba saraAwiylahu fata$am~ara [ He drew together the tuck of his drawers, or trousers, &c., and prepared himself for active employment ]: (O and TA, from a trad.:) and the part so drawn together &c. is called the vubonap . (IAar, O.) -A2- See also A^uEotiba , said of a bone. -A3- Et~b is also said of a man as meaning He was, or became, slow, tardy, dilatory, late, or backward: in which sense, its b is thought by ISd to be a substitute for the m in Eat~ama . (TA.)

definition: He asked him, petitioned him, or solicited him, to grant him his good will, or favour;
sourceDefinition: He asked him, petitioned him, or solicited him, to grant him his good will, or favour; to regard him with good will, or favour; to become well pleased, content, or satisfied, with him; (S, O, K;) or he desired, or sought, of him that he should return to making him happy, or to doing what was pleasing to him, from doing evil to him. (S.) And AstEtb , alone, He asked, solicited, sought, or desired, good will, or favour; or to be regarded with good will, or favour. (S, Msb.) walaA humo yusotaEotabuwna , in the Kur xvi. 86, and xxx. 57, and xlv. 34. means Nor shall they be asked to return to what will please God. (Jel.) And waA_ino yasotaEotibuwA famaA humo mina A@lomuEotabiyna , in the Kur xli. 23, means And if they solicit God's favour, they shall not be regarded with favour: (Jel:) or if they petition their Lord to cancel their compact, [or to restore them to the world, He will not do so; i. e.] He will not restore them to the world; (O, K, TA;) knowing that, if they were restored, they would return to that which they have been forbidden to do: this is the meaning if we read the verb in the active form: otherwise, (O, TA,) reading yusotaEotabuwA [and muEotibiyna ], as 'Obeyd Ibn-'Omeyr did, (O,) the meaning is, If God cancelled their compact, and restored them to the world, they would not [ return from their evil ways, and ] act obediently to God: (O, TA:) [for] ― -b2- AisotaEotabotuhu also signifies I asked him, or desired him, to cancel a bargain, or compact, with me. (TA.) -A2- See also 4, in three places.

definition: The being well pleased, content, or satis- fied, [with a person,] or the regarding with good will, or favour: (M, A, K:) or good pleasure, content, satisfaction, good will, or favour: (MA, K, KL:)...
sourceDefinition: The being well pleased, content, or satis- fied, [with a person,] or the regarding with good will, or favour: (M, A, K:) or good pleasure, content, satisfaction, good will, or favour: (MA, K, KL:) its primary signification is the returning of one whose good will, or favour, has been solicited, or desired, to the love of his companion: (TA:) it is the subst. from A^aEotabaniY as meaning “ he returned to making me happy, ” &c.; (S; see 4;) a subst. from AlA_iEotaAbu ; (Msb;) [i. e.] it is put in the place of AEtAb ; and [thus] it signifies [the returning to making one happy, or doing what is pleasing to him, from doing evil to him: or] the returning, from doing evil, to that which makes the person who has reproved, or blamed, or been angry, to be well pleased, content, or satisfied: and [simply] the returning from doing a crime, a misdeed, an offence, or an evil action. (TA.) One says, A^aEoTaAniY AlEutobaY He granted me his good will, or favour. (A.) And A_in~amaA yuEaAtabu mano turojaY Einodahu AlEutobaY Only he should be reproved in whom the [finding a disposition to a] return from his evil conduct may be hoped for. (TA.) And AlEutobaY is [said to be] used when one does not mean thereby AlA_iEotaAb , (S, O, TA,) i. e. in the contr. of its primary sense, (TA,) in the prov. laka AlEutobaY biA^ano laA raDiyta i. e. [ bilaA riDaAka , as though meaning Thou shalt have content, or satisfaction, without thy being well pleased; or] I will content thee with the contrary of what thou likest: and in like manner the corresponding verb is [said to be] used in the verse of Bishr Ibn-Abee-Kházim cited above in the explanations of that verb: (S, O, TA:) [but the prov. here mentioned may be well rendered thou shalt return from thine evil way against thy wish; for,] accord. to Fr, AlEutobaY in the phrase laka lEutobaY signifies the returning, from what one like, to what he dislikes: (MF:) and it signifies also [as expl. above] the returning from doing a crime, a misdeed, &c. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. Eu*orN (S, O, Msb, K) and Eu*urN (S, O, K) and Eu*oraY (O, K) and maEo*irapN and maEo*urapN (K) [all of which are also used as simple substs.]; and ↓ AE*rhu ; (S, O, Msb, K;) He excused him; freed, cleared, or exempted, him from blame; exculpated him: (Msb:) or he accepted his excuse: properly, Ea*arotu signifies I cancelled evil conduct. (TA.) [See also Eu*orN below.] You say, Ea*arotuhu fiymaA SanaEa (S, O, Msb) I excused, or exculpated, him for what he did. (Msb.) And in a trad. of El-Mikdád it is said, A@ll~`hu A_ilayoka ↓ laqado A^aEo*ara i.e. Verily God hath excused thee, and exempted thee from the obligation to fight against the unbelievers; for he had become extremely fat, and unable to fight. (TA.) And you say [also], Ea*arahu Eani Al$~aYo'i He excused him for, or from, the thing. (MA.) [And accord. to Golius, Ea*arahu EalaY Al$~aYo'i , as well as fiY Al$~aYo'i : but he has not mentioned his authority: see an explanation of Ea*iyrN , from which the former phrase was perhaps derived by him.] And Ea*arotuhu mino fulaAnK [ I excused him, or held him excusable, for his conduct to such a one ]; meaning, I did not blame him, but I blamed such a one. (S, * TA.) And mano yaEo*iruniY minohu Who will excuse me, or make my excuse, if I requite him (Msb, TA) for his action, (Msb,) or for his evil action, (TA,) and will not blame me (Msb, TA) for it? (Msb:) or who will excuse me with respect to his case, and will not blame me for it? (Msb.) [And a similar ex. is mentioned in the TA with fiY in the place of mino .] ― -b2- [Hence,] Ea*ara , (Az, S, IKtt, O, Msb, K,) aor. ; (O, TA;) and ↓ AE*r , (S, IKtt, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_iEo*aArN ; (TA;) He was vitious, or faulty, and corrupt: (Msb:) or he was guilty of many crimes, sins, faults, offences, or acts of disobedience, (S, O, Msb, K,) so as to vender him excusable who punished him. (TA.) It is said in a trad., lano yaholika Aln~aAsu Hat~aY yaEo*iruwA mino A^anofusihimo , (O, and so in some copies of the S and K,) or ↓ yuEo*iruwA , (so in other copies of the S and K, ) both of which readings are the same in meaning, (TA,) i. e. [ Men will not perish, or die, ] until they are guilty of many crimes, or sins, &c.; (S, O, Msb, K;) meaning, (accord. to A 'Obeyd, S, O,) until they deserve punishment, so as to render excusable him who punishes them. (S, A, O, TA.) And you say, mino nafosihi ↓ AE*r , meaning He placed himself within the power of another. (TA.) -A2- And Ea*arotuhu I aided him, or assisted him, against an enemy. (Msb.) -A3- Ea*ara , inf. n. Ea*orN , He cut, or cut off. (TA: but only the inf. n. of the verb in this sense is there mentioned.) ― -b2- And [hence, probably, as is implied in a passage in the TA, (see Eu*orapN ,)] Ea*ara , aor. , (S, O, * Msb, K) inf. n. Ea*orN ; (S, Msb;) and ↓ AE*r ; (S, O, Msb, K;) both as expl. by A 'Obeyd; (S;) (tropical:) He circumcised a boy, (S, O, Msb, K,) and in like manner a girl; (S, O, Msb;) but when a girl is the object, xafaDa is more common. (S, O.) -A4- Ea*ara Alfarasa biAlEi*aAri , aor. and ; and ↓ AE*rhu ; He fastened, or bound, the horse's Ei*aAr [q. v.]: (S, O, K:) and Alfarasa ↓ AE*r he bridled the horse; syn. sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taEo*iyrN , He was without excuse; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ EA*r , (K, TA,) inf. n. muEaA*arapN : (TA:) he affected to excuse himself, but had no excuse: he excused himself, but did not adduce an excuse [ that was valid ]. (TA.) [See also 8.] ― -b2- And He was remiss, wanting, deficient, or defective, (S, O, Msb, TA,) in an affair, (S, Msb,) setting up an excuse [ for being so ]; (O;) fell short, or did less than was incumbent on him, (S, O, Msb, TA,) in it; (S, Msb;) did not exert himself, or act vigorously, in it; (Msb, TA;) causing it to be imagined that he had an excuse when he had none. (Bd in ix. 91.) You say, qaAma fulaAnN qiyaAma taEo*iyrK Such a one acted remissly, falling short, or doing less than was incumbent on him. (TA.) And it is said in a story of the Children of Israel, nahaAhumo A^aHobaAruhumo taEo*iyrFA Their learned men forbade them remissly: the inf. n. being here put in the place of the act. part. n. as a denotative of state; as it is in jaA='a ma$oyFA . (O, TA.) [See also 4.] -A2- Also (tropical:) He made, or prepared, a feast, (O, K,) such as is termed A_iEo*aAr [q. v.] (O) or Ei*aAr : (K:) and he invited to a feast such as is thus termed. (K. [Accord. to the TA, these are two distinct significations of the verb. See, again, 4.]) -A3- E*~r Alfarasa : see 1, latter half, in two places. ― -b2- Ea*~iro Ean~iY baEiyraka , (S, O,) and Ean~iY ↓ A^aEo*irohu , (O,) Brand thy camel with a brand different from that of mine, in order that our camels may be known, one from the other. (S, O.) ― -b3- E*~r AlgulaAmu The hair of the boy's Ei*aAr (K, TA) i. e. of his cheek (TA) grew. (K, TA.) -A4- E*~r Ald~aAra (inf. n. as above, TA) He effaced the traces of the house, or dwelling. (K, TA.) -A5- E*~rhu , (S, O, K,) inf. n. as above, (S, O,) He defiled, or besmeared, it (a thing, K) with Ea*irap [or human dung ]. (S, O, K.)

sourceDefinition: : see 1, in five places from the commencement. ― -b2- Also He had an excuse; [or he was, or became, excusable; ] (S, O, K;) and so ↓ AEt*r . (S, O, K.) It is said in a prov., A^aEo*ara mano A^ano*ara [ He has an excuse, or is excusable, who warns ]. (S. [See also below: and see art. n*r . It is held by some in the present day that the A in AE*r , in this phrase, has a privative effect, and that the meaning is, He deprives of excuse who warns: but for this I have not found any authority.]) And Lebeed says, (S, O, TA,) addressing his two daughters, (O, TA,) and telling them to wail and weep a year for him after his death, (TA,) A_ilaY AlHawoli vum~a A@somu Als~alaAmi EalayokumaA ↓ wamano yaboki HawolFA kaAmilFA faqado A@Eota*aro [ Until the end of the year: then the name of peace be an you both: for such as weeps a whole year has become excusable ]. (S, O.) You say also, A^aEo*arotu Einoda Als~uloTaAni I got excuse of the Sultán [or ruling power ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And He manifested an excuse: (K, TA:) in which sense, Eu*orN is said to be its inf. n., as well as A_iEo*aArN ; but the former is correctly a simple subst. (TA.) And He pleaded that by which he should be excused. (TA.) [See also 8.] ― -b4- He did that by which he should be excused. (TA.) ― -b5- He did that in which he should be excused: hence the saying of Zuheyr, * satamonaEukumo A^aromaAHunaA A^awo sanuEo*iru [ Our spears shall prevent you, or shall defend you, ] or we will do that in which we shall be excused. (S, O: but in the latter, watamonaEukumo .) ― -b6- And He exceeded the usual bounds, (A, Mgh, O,) or went to the utmost point, (TA,) in excuse, (A, Mgh, O, TA,) i. e. in being excused. (A.) So in the saying A^aEo*ara mano A^ano*ara [ He exceeds the usual bounds in rendering himself excused who warns ]. (A, Mgh, O. [See also above, third sentence.]) And it is said in a trad., laqado A^aEo*ara A@ll~`hu A_ilaY mano balaga mina AlEumuri sit~iyna sanapF [app. meaning Verily God hath freed himself from the imputation of injustice to an extraordinary degree, or to the utmost point, to him who hath attained sixty years of age: ] i. e. He hath left him no plea for excuse [for his sins], since He hath granted him respite for all this length of time and he hath not excused himself. (TA. [As AE*r is here followed by A_ilaY , I do not think that this explanation is meant to show that the A has a privative effect, and that the verb signifies “ he deprived of excuse. ”]) ― -b7- [Hence,] He exerted himself, acted vigorously, took extraordinary pains, or exceeded the usual bounds, [ so as to render himself excused, ] (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) fiY AlA^amori in the affair; (S, O, Msb;) as, for instance, in eating, in relation to which it occurs in a trad., wherein one is enjoined to do so when eating with others, [app. meaning with guests and with a host,] such having been the custom of the Prophet; for, when he ate with others, he was the last in eating. (TA.) [Hence also,] A^aEo*arotu A_ilayoka I took extraordinary pains, or exceeded the usual bounds, in exhortation and precept to thee. (TA.) ― -b8- And He was remiss, wanting, deficient, or defective; he fell short, or did less than was incumbent on him; feigning ( yuriY [in the CK, erroneously, yurY` ]) that he was doing the contrary: as though the verb bore two contrary significations. (K.) [See also 2.] -A2- Also I. q. A^anoSafa : (O, K:) you say, A^aEo*ironiY mino h`*aA i. e. A^anoSifoniY minohu [ Give thou me, or obtain for me, my right, or due, from this person]: and hence the saying of the Prophet to Aboo-Bekr, respecting 'Áïsheh, A^aEo*ironiY minohaA A_ino A^ad~abotuhaA [ Obtain thou for me my right, or due, from her if I discipline her, or chastise her ]: (O:) or this means undertake thou to excuse me [ for my conduct to her &c.]: (TA:) and the Arabs say, A^aEo*ara fulaAnN mino nafosihi [ Such a one became bound to render an excuse for his conduct to himself; (see Ea*iyrN ;)] meaning such a one was destroyed by himself. (Yoo, TA.) -A3- As signifying He circumcised: see 1, latter half. It is said in a trad., kun~aA A_iEo*aAra yawomK waAHidK , meaning We were circumcised in one day. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) He made a feast on the occasion of a circumcision, (AZ, Msb, K, TA,) liloqawomi for the people, or party: (K:) he prepared such a feast: from the same verb signifying “ he circumcised. ” (TA.) [See also 2: and see A_iEo*aArN as a subst.] -A4- AE*r Alfarasa and All~ijaAma : see 1, latter half, in five places. ― -b2- And A^aEo*iro Ean~iY baEiyraka : see 2, near the end. ― -b3- A^aEo*iro EalaY naSiybika Make a mark upon thy share. (O.) ― -b4- AE*r fiY Zahorihi He beat him (O, K) with whips (O) so as to make a mark, or marks, upon his back. (O, K.) And Darabahu Hat~aY A^aEo*ara matonahu He beat him so that he made the beating heavy upon his back and obtained from him relief from his anger. (TA.) And Duriba faA^uEo*ira , (S, O, K,) in the Tahdheed of IKtt faA^aEo*ara , (TA,) He (a man) was beaten so that he was at the point of death. (S, O, K, TA.) And A^uEo*ira minohu He had wounds inflicted upon him so that fear was excited for him in consequence thereof. (O.) And A^aEo*ara bihi He, or it, left a scar upon him. (O, * TA.) ― -b5- And A^aEo*arotu Ald~aAra and fiY Ald~aAri I made a mark, or marks, in, or upon, the house, or dwelling. (O.) -A5- AE*r also signifies He (a man, TA) voided his ordure. (O, K.) ― -b2- And AE*rt Ald~aAru The house, or dwelling, had in it much Ea*irap [or human ordure ]. (S, O.)

And Duriba faA^uEo*ira , (S, O, K,) in the Tahdheed of IKtt faA^aEo*ara , (TA,) He (a man) was beaten so that he was at the point of death. (S, O, K, TA.) (O, * TA.) ― -b5- And A^aEo*arotu Ald~aAra and fiY Ald~aAri I made a mark, or marks, in, or upon, the house, or dwelling. (O.) -A5- AE*r also signifies He (a man, TA) voided his ordure. (O, K.) ― -b2- And AE*rt Ald~aAru The house, or dwelling, had in it much Ea*irap [or human ordure ]. (S, O.)

[See Eu*orN .] You say, AEt*r A_ilaY~a [ He excused himself to me; ] he begged me to accept his excuse; (Msb;) and AZ says, I have heard two Arabs of the desert, one of the tribe of Temeem and one of the tribe of Keys, say, A_ilaY ↓ taEa*~arotu Alr~ajuli in the sense of AiEota*arotu [i. e. (O, K.) ― -b2- See also 5, last sentence but one, in two places. -A4- And AEt*r AlEimaAmapa He made the turban to have two portions [ its two ends ] hanging down behind. (O, K.) -A5- And AlAiEoti*aAru signifies also The act of devirginating. (S, O, [See Eu*orapN .])

definition: He asked, or desired, to be excused if he should lay violent hands upon such a one [or requite him for an evil action ];
sourceDefinition: He asked, or desired, to be excused if he should lay violent hands upon such a one [or requite him for an evil action ]; he said, mano Ea*iyriY mino fulaAnK . (A, TA.) (A, O, TA.)

definition: (Msb, K) and ↓ Eu*urN (Msb) and ↓ Ei*orapN (S, O, K) and ↓ Eu*oraY (S, Msb) and ↓ maEo*irapN (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ maEo*urapN and ↓ maEo*arapN (K) [all as simple substs.
sourceDefinition: (Msb, K) and ↓ Eu*urN (Msb) and ↓ Ei*orapN (S, O, K) and ↓ Eu*oraY (S, Msb) and ↓ maEo*irapN (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ maEo*urapN and ↓ maEo*arapN (K) [all as simple substs., but all except the third and the last mentioned also as inf. ns.,] An excuse; an apology; a plea whereby one excuses himself [or another ]: accord. to the B, Eu*orN [as a subst. from AiEota*ara or from A^aEo*ara ] is of three kinds; the saying “ I did it not; ” and the saying “ I did it for such a cause, ” mentioning what might exempt him from being culpable; and the saying “ I did it, but will not do it again, ” or the like; which third kind is the same as tawobapN : (TA:) the pl. of Eu*orN is A^aEo*aArN ; (Msb, K;) and that of ↓ Ei*orapN is Ei*arN ; (O;) and that of ↓ mE*rp is [ maEaA*iru , and, irregularly,] maEaA*iyru : (TA:) and ↓ Ea*iyrN , of which Eu*orN , (Ksh,) or ↓ Eu*urN , (Bd,) may be pl., is syn. with [ Eu*orN and] mE*rp ; (Ksh and Bd in lxxvii. 6;) and ↓ miEo*aArN is [likewise] syn. with Eu*orN . (Bd in lxxv. 15.) It is said in a prov., makaA*ibu ↓ AlmaEaA*iru [ Excuses are lies ]. (TA.) And it was said by Ibráheem En-Nakha'ee, ya$uwbuhaA ↓ A_in~a AlmaEaA*iyra Alka*ibu [ Verily excuses, lying mixes therewith ]. (S, O.) ― -b2- Eu*orFA A^awo nu*orFA , in the Kur [lxxvii. 6], or A^awo nu*urFA , ↓ Eu*urFA , (Bd,) means For excusing or terrifying; the two ns. being inf. ns.: or for excuses or warnings; the two ns. being pls., of ↓ Ea*iyrN in the sense of mE*rp and of na*iyrN in the sense A_ino*aArN : or such as excuse and such as warn; the two ns. being pls. of ↓ EaA*irN and muno*irN : (Ksh, Bd:) or, accord. to Th, both mean the same. (TA.) [See also nu*orN .] ― -b3- And the Arabs say, laA nu*oraAka ↓ Eu*oraAka i. e. A^aEo*iro walaA tuno*iro [app. meaning Do that for which thou wilt be excused, by inflicting punishment when it is deserved, and do not merely warn, and put in fear ]. (TA in art. n*r .) -A2- Eu*orN also signifies Success; or the attainment, or accomplishment, of one's wants, or of a thing: (IAar, O, K:) and victory, or success in a contest. (O, K.) One says, with respect to a war or a battle, limana AlEu*oru Whose is the success, or victory? (O.) -A3- See also Eu*orapN , in five places: and see Ei*aArN , last quarter.

sourceDefinition: The virginity, maidenhead, or hymen; syn. bakaArapN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) or qiD~apN ; so called from Ea*orN signifying the “ act of cutting, ” because a girl's hymen ( xaAtamu Eu*oratihaA ) is rent when she is devirginated; (Lh, Az, TA;) AlEu*orapu being that whereby a girl is a virgin: (Lh, TA:) [and ↓ Eu*orN perhaps signifies the same: (see an ex. voce A^ariymN ; and see also the next sentence here following:)] pl. Eu*arN . (Msb.) ― -b2- And Devirgination of a girl [or woman]: (Lh, K:) [and ↓ Eu*orN is used in the same sense:] one says, fulaAnN A^abuw Eu*orihaA (S, A, O, K) and Abw Eu*oratihaA (TA) (tropical:) [lit. Such a one is the father, i. e. the author, of her devirgination ]; meaning such a one is he who devirginated her. (S, A, O, K, TA.) And [hence] one says also, h`*aA AlkalaAmi ↓ huwa A^abuw Ea*ori (tropical:) [ He was the first utterer of this speech ]. (A.) And maA h`*aA AlkalaAmi ↓ A^anota bi*iY Eu*ori (tropical:) Thou art not the first utterer of this speech. (S, O, TA. [But see an assertion of Sb cited voce $iEorN .]) ― -b3- And The [ part in the external organs of generation of a girl or woman termed ] baZor [q. v.]; (K;) the place of a girl where the operation of circumcision is performed: so called from Ea*orN signifying the “ act of cutting. ” (Lh, Az, TA.) [See also AlEaA*uwru .] ― -b4- And The prepuce of a boy: (O, K:) so accord. to Lh, who does not say whether it be so called before or after it has been cut off: said by others to be the portion of skin which the circumciser cuts off. (TA.) ― -b5- And Circumcision; syn. xitaAnN . (K.) One says, danaA waqotu Eu*orapi AlS~abiY~i The time of the circumcision of the boy drew near. (TK.) ― -b6- And A sign, or mark; syn. EalaAmapN ; (O, K, TA;) as also ↓ Eu*orN . (TA.) See also Ei*aArN , last quarter. ― -b7- And The hair upon the withers of a horse: (S, O, K:) and, (K,) accord. to As, (S, O,) a lock, or small quantity, of hair: (S, O, K:) and the naASiyap [or forelock of a horse]; (K;) the hair of the naASiyap of a horse: (A:) or, accord. to some, the mane of a horse: (TA:) pl. Eu*arN : (S, O, TA:) which is said by some to mean hairs [ extending ] from the back of the head to the middle of the neck: (TA:) and, as pl. of Eu*orapN , a sign, mark, or token, that is tied to the forelock of a horse that outstrips, [ as a preservative ] from the [ evil ] eye. (Ham p. 795.) ― -b8- And AlEu*orapu is the appellation of Five stars at the extremity of the Milky Way: (S, O, K:) or, as some say, below Sirius, and also called ↓ AlEa*aAraY , [app. the star e of Canis Major (which is called by our astronomers “ adara, ” often written “ adard, ”) with four other neighbouring stars, ] which rise [ aurorally ] in the midst of the heat: (TA:) and, (O, K, TA,) as some say, (O, TA,) AlEu*orapu is a star at the time of the [ auroral ] rising of which the heat becomes intense; (O, K, TA;) [app. the star h of Canis Major (which is called by our astronomers “ aludra ”);] it rises [ aurorally, in Central Arabia, in the latter part of July O. S., ] after Sirius and before Canopus, and is accompanied with intense heat, without wind, taking away the breath. (O, TA.) ― -b9- Also (i. e. AlEu*orapu ) Pain in the fauces, (Mgh, K,) [ arising ] from the blood; (Mgh;) as also ↓ AlEaA*uwru , (K, accord. to the TA,) or ↓ AlEaAduwraA='u ; (thus in some copies of the K, and thus accord. to the CK;) or pain of the fauces, (S, O, K,) in a part near the uvula, (S, O,) [ arising ] from the blood: (S, O, K:) it is said to be a small swelling, or pustule, that comes forth in the xarom [app. meaning the uvula, as being a projection from the soft palate,] which is between the fauces and the nose: it is incident to children, at the time of the [ auroral ] rising of AlEu*orap , i. e. the star that rises after Sirius, mentioned above; and on the occasion thereof, a woman has recourse to a piece of rag, which she twists tightly, and inserts into the nose so as to pierce that place, whereupon there issues from it black blood, and sometimes it becomes ulcerated; and this piercing is called Ald~agoru : then they suspended to the child some such thing as the [amulet termed] Euw*ap . (TA. [See 1 in art. dgr .]) ― -b10- It also signifies The place of the pain above mentioned, (S, O, K,) which is near the uvula. (S, O.)

definition: Human dung or ordure;
sourceDefinition: Human dung or ordure; (S, * O, * Msb, K, TA;) as also ↓ EaA*irN (IAar, IDrd, O, L, K, TA) and ↓ EaA*irapN : (O, K:) pl. of the first [which is the most common] Ea*iraAtN , (Msb,) and of ↓ the second Eu*arN . (IAar, TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (S, O, Msb,) (tropical:) The court, or yard, ( finaA=' ,) of a house: (S, O, Msb, K, TA:) so called because the human ordure ( AlEa*irap ) used to be cast in it: (S, O, Msb:) or, accord. to As, this is the primary signification; what is before mentioned being so termed because cast in the fnA' ; like as it is termed gaAy^iT because cast in the EAy^T , which means “ a depressed piece of ground; ” (Har p. 403;) [and] thus says A 'Obeyd: pl. as above: (O, TA:) and maEaA*iru [pl. of ↓ maEo*arN which lit. signifies a place of human dung or ordure ] is syn. with Ea*iraAtN as meaning A^afoniyapN [pl. of finaA='N ]. (Ham p. 677, q. v.) It is related of 'Alee that he reproved some persons, and said, maA lakumo laA tunaZ~ifuwna Ea*iraAtikumo (A, * O, TA) i. e. (tropical:) [ What aileth you that ye will not cleanse ] the courts, or yards, of your houses? (TA.) And in a trad. (O, TA) of the Prophet (O) it is said, Alyahuwdu A^anotanu xaloqi A@ll~`hi Ea*irapF , (A, O, TA,) which may mean (tropical:) [ The Jews are the most stinking of God's creatures ] in respect of the court, or yard, of the house: or in respect of ordure. (TA.) And it is said in a prov., A_in~ahu labariYo'u AlEa*irapi , a phrase like bariYo'u Als~aAHapi (tropical:) [lit. Verily he is clear in respect of the court, or yard, of the house; app. meaning, clear of disgrace ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) A place where people sit (K, TA) in the court, or yard, of the house. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) The worst of what come forth from wheat or corn ( TaEaAm ), (Lh, O, K, TA,) and is thrown away, (Lh, TA,) when it is cleared; (O;) as also Ea*ibapN . (Lh, TA.)

definition: A virgin: (S, O, K:) used as an epithet: you say jaAriyapN Ea*oraA='u a virgin girl: (TA:) and AimoraA^apN Ea*oraA='u , meaning *aAtu Ea*orapK : (Msb:) accord.
sourceDefinition: A virgin: (S, O, K:) used as an epithet: you say jaAriyapN Ea*oraA='u a virgin girl: (TA:) and AimoraA^apN Ea*oraA='u , meaning *aAtu Ea*orapK : (Msb:) accord. to IAar alone, so called liDiyqihaA , from taEa*~ara Ealayohi AlA^amoru : (TA:) pl. Ea*aAraY and Ea*aArK [with the art. AlEa*aAriY , and thus written in the S and O and K] (S, O, K, TA) and Ea*oraAwaAtN , (S, O, K,) like SaHaAraY [&c.]. (S, O.) ― -b2- [Hence,] AlEa*oraA='u (assumed tropical:) [ The sign Virgo; ] the sign Als~unobulapu : or AljawozaA='u [which is an evident mistake]. (K.) ― -b3- And AlEa*aAraY (assumed tropical:) Certain stars, described above: see Eu*orapN , latter half. ― -b4- And A^aSaAbiEu AlEa*aAraY (assumed tropical:) A sort of grapes, black and long, like acorns; likened to the dyed fingers of virgins. (TA.) ― -b5- And dur~apN Ea*oraA='u (tropical:) A pearl not bored. (A, O, K, * TA.) ― -b6- And ramolapN Ea*oraA='u (tropical:) A sand upon which one has not trodden (A, O, K, * TA) nor ridden, because of its height. (TA.) ― -b7- And AlEa*oraA='u (assumed tropical:) A kind of collar by means of which the hands, or arms, are confined together with the neck: (T, O, TA:) or such as is put upon the throat of a man and has not been put upon the neck of any one before: (TA:) or a thing of iron by means of which a man is tortured in order to make him confess an affair, or the like; (K, TA;) as, for instance, for the purpose of extorting property &c.: pl. Ea*aAraY . (TA.) [Compare the term “ maiden ” applied to an instrument for beheading.] ― -b8- Also a name of [ El-Medeeneh, ] the City of the Prophet: (K, TA:) because of its not having been abased. (TA.)

definition: A certain appertenance of a horse or the like;
sourceDefinition: A certain appertenance of a horse or the like; (S, O;) i. e. the part, (T, M, Mgh,) or strap, (Msb,) of the bridle, (T, M, Mgh, Msb,) that lies, (T,) or extends down, (M, K,) upon the cheek, (M, Mgh, Msb, K,) or two cheeks, (T,) of the horse (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K) or the like: (T, Mgh, Msb:) the Ea*aAraAni are the two straps upon the two cheeks of the horse, on the right and left: (IDrd in his Book on the Saddle and Bridle:) or, as some say, the Ei*aAr is the two straps of the bridle that meet at the back of the neck: (TA:) [thus it signifies either of the two cheek-straps, or, accord. to some, the two cheek-straps together, that compose the headstall: ] some say that it is called by the name of its place; but the converse is the case accord. to others: (TA:) [and Ei*aAru Alr~asani signifies the appertance, of the halter, corresponding to the cheek-strap, or cheek-straps, of the bridle or headstall: (see a verse of Ibn-Mukbil cited voce rasanN :)] pl. Eu*urN , (S, O, Msb, K, [in the CK Eu*orN ,]) like as kutubN is pl. of kitaAbN . (Msb, TA.) It is said in a trad., lalofaqoru A^azoyanu lilomuw^omini mino Ei*aArK HasanK EalaY xad~i farasK [ Verily poverty is more ornamental to the believer than a beautiful cheek-strap, or headstall, upon the cheek of a horse ]. (TA.) farasN qaSiyru AlEi*aAri [ A horse short in the cheek-strap, or headstall, ] implies commendation, as denoting width of the lip. (TA, voce EinaAnN .) And Ei*aArN signifies also The thing that connects the leading-rope ( Habola AlxiTaAmi ) to the head of the he-camel (K, TA) and of the she-camel. (TA.) And A halter; syn. rasanN : (Msb:) and ↓ muEa*~arN signifies a halter ( rasan ) having a double Ei*aAr ( *uw Ei*aArayoni ). (TA.) One says, fulaAnN $adiydu AlEi*aAri (assumed tropical:) Such a one is strong in respect of determination. (A, TA.) And fulaAnN xaliyEu AlEi*aAri (assumed tropical:) Such a one is weak in respect of determination; [or is a person who has thrown off restraint; ] like a horse that has no bridle upon him, and that therefore falls upon his face. sourceDefinition: : see Eu*orN , in two places. ― -b2- Also i. q. ↓ EaA*irN [act. part. n. of 1, Excusing; an excuser; &c.]. (K.) You say, mano Ea*iyriY mino fulaAnK Who will excuse me, or make my excuse, or be my excuser, if I requite such a one (Msb, TA) for his action, (Msb,) or for his evil action, (TA,) and will not blame me (Msb, TA) for it? or who will excuse me with respect to the case of such a one, and not blame me for it? (Msb: [see Ea*arotuhu mino fulaAnK : and see also 10:]) or who will aid me, or assist me, against such a one, or to defend myself from him? (Msb;) who will be my aider, or assistant, against such a one? (TA:) for Ea*iyrN is also said to signify an aider, or assister, against an enemy. (Msb, K, TA.) The Prophet said thus with respect to 'Abd-Allah Ibn-Ubeí, demanding of the people that they should excuse him for laying violent hands upon him. (TA.) [It is a phrase by which one asks for permission to retaliate, or punish, &c.] And one says also, Ea*iyraka mino fulaAnK , meaning Bring him who will excuse thee [ for what thou hast done, or doest, or wilt do, to such a one ]; (S, O, TA;) i. e. bring him who will blame him and will not blame thee. (S, O.) And Ea*yraka A_iy~aAYa minohu Bring thine excuse of me [ for what I have done, &c., to him ]. (TA.) A poet (Dhu-l-Isba' El-'Adwánee, O, TA) says, Ea*iyra AlHaY~i mino EadowaA na kaAnuwA Hay~apa AlA^aroDi bagaY baEoDN EalaY baEoDK falamo yaroEuwoA EalaY baEoDi faqado A^aDoHawoA A^aHaAdiyva birafoEi Alqawoli waAlxafoDi (S, * O, * L, TA) [Bring an excuse for the tribe, for what they have done to 'Adwán, i. e., one to another; for the tribe of 'Adwán were rent by intestine wars, in which Dhu-l-Isba' took a prominent part; (see the Essai sur l' Histoire des Arabes by Caussin de Perceval, vol. ii. p. 262;) therefore we may render the phrase, bring an excuse for the tribe, 'Adwán, regarding mino as redundant in this instance, like as it is in faA@jotanibuwA A@lr~ijosa mina A@loA^awovaAni , in the Kur xxii. 31; and then proceed thus: they were the serpent of the earth (meaning cunning, guileful, malignant, or mischievous, and strong, not neglecting to take blood-revenge, as expl. in art. HY in the TA): but some acted wrongfully against some, and were not regardful of the rights of some: so they became subjects of talk uttered by the raising of speech and the lowering thereof]: he means, bring an excuse for what some of them have done to some by mutual hatred and slaughter, some of them being not regardful of some; after their having been the serpent of the earth, which every one fears. (L, TA.) ― -b3- Also A state, or condition, ( HAl ,) which one desires, or seeks after, for which, or on account of which, he is to be excused ( yuEo*aru EalayohaA ): (S, O, K, TA:) [and in one of my copies of the S is added, A_i*aA faEalahaA , as though by HAl were here meant an action: ] pl. Eu*urN , sometimes, in poetry, contracted into Eu*orN . (S, O.) El-'Ajjáj said, (S, O, TA,) in reply to his wife, who, seeing him repairing the saddle of his she-camel for a journey which he had determined to make, asked him, “ What is this that thou repairest ? ” (TA,) jaAriYa laA tasotanokiriY Ea*iyriY saEoyiY waA_i$ofaAqiY EalaY baEiyriY (S, O,) or, as some relate it, sayoriY wA$fAqY , (O,) [i. e. O girl, inquire not as disapproving it respecting my desired state for which I shall be excusable (or rather my excusable purpose ), my work (or my journeying ), and my benevolent care for my camel; ] meaning yaA jaAriyapu , [and suppressing yA ] and apocopating [ jAryp ]. (S, O. [In the TA, AlbaEiyri is put for baEiyriY .]) -A2- See also EaA*irN : -A3- and A_iEo*aArN .

definition: One excusing himself, whether he have, or have not, an excuse: (TA:) the person to whom this epithet is applied may be a speaker of truth, and he may be not a speaker of truth: (Msb, TA:) and so ↓...
sourceDefinition: One excusing himself, whether he have, or have not, an excuse: (TA:) the person to whom this epithet is applied may be a speaker of truth, and he may be not a speaker of truth: (Msb, TA:) and so ↓ muEa*~irN , which, as applied to a speaker of truth, signifies having an excuse, like muEota*irN , (S, O, K,) [of which it is a variation,] for the t is changed into * , and this is incorporated [into the radical * ], and its vowel is transferred to the E , like as is the case in yaxaS~imuwna ; (S, O;) and ↓ muEi*~irN is also allowable, (S, O, TA,) and also ↓ muEu*~irN ; (S, O;) but [it is said that] ↓ muEa*~irN applied to him who does not speak truth, (S, O, K,) being [originally] of the measure mufaE~ilN , [not a variation of muEota*irN ,] (S, O,) means falling short, or doing less than is incumbent on him, (S, O, K,) excusing himself (S, O) without having any [ real or valid ] excuse. (S, O, K.) In the Kur ix. 91, I'Ab read ↓ AlmuEo*iruwna [instead of the more usual reading ↓ AlmuEa*~iruwna ], (S, O, K,) and so did Yaakoob El-Hadramee, (Az, TA,) from A^aEo*ara ; the former asserting that it was so revealed; app. considering ↓ muEa*~irN , with teshdeed, to apply to one not speaking truth, (S, O, K,) meaning pretending to excuse himself, without having any real excuse; (S, O;) and ↓ muEo*irN to mean having an excuse: (S, O, K:) Ibn-Abee-Leylà and Tá-oos read ↓ AlmuEaA*iruwna , as meaning those striving, or labouring, in seeking excuse. (O.)

definition: , (S, A, O, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, A, O, Msb,) inf. n. Eas~N (S, O, Msb, K) and EasasN ; (S, O, K;) and ↓ AEts~ ; (S, O, K;) He went roundabout, patrolled, or went the rounds, by night, (S, A, O, K,) to guard the people: (TA:) he made search by night after suspicious persons, or persons to be suspected, (S, A, O, Msb, K,) and investi- gated, or discovered, their opinions, or sentiments: (TA:) he went to and fro; syn. Aixotalafa . (Ham p. 320.) It is said in a prov., kalobN Eas~a xayorN mino kalobK rabaDa , (S, O,) or ↓ A@Eotas~a ; (O, K;) or, as some relate it, EaAs~N , and raAbiDK ; (TA;) [ A dog that has gone the rounds by night is better than a dog that has lain down; or a dog going the rounds &c.;] said for the purpose of urging to make gain: meaning that he who occupies himself in business is better than he who lacks power or ability: (TA:) or, as some relate it, kalobN Eas~a xayorN mino A^asadK A@nodas~a [ a dog that has gone the rounds by night is better than a lion that has hidden himself ]; alluding to the superiority of the weak who occupies himself in making gain over the strong who holds back. (O, TA.) You also say of a wolf, (S, O, K,) and of any beast of prey, (TA,) ↓ EasoEasa , meaning, He went roundabout by night, (S, O, K, TA,) seeking for prey: (TA:) and ↓ taEasoEasa he (a wolf, TA) sought for prey (S, O, K, TA) by night: (S, TA:) and ↓ AEts~ he [a man] sought, sought after, or sought to gain, sustenance: (S, O, K:) and ↓ taEasoEasa he (a wolf, AA, S) smelt [app. to find prey ]. (AA, S, O, K. *) -A2- Eas~a xabaruhu , (S, L, K,) aor. , inf. n. Eas~N , (L, TA,) His tidings were slow, or tardy. (S, L, K, TA. [In the O, xayoruhu .]) ― -b2- Eas~ato , aor. , She (a camel) yielded little milk, though her milk had collected in her udder since the next previous milking. (TA.) ― -b3- And Eas~ato , aor. , inf. n. EisaAsN , She (a camel) grumbled much on being milked. (TA.) Hence, dar~ato EisaAsFA She yielded her milk unwillingly. (IDrd, O, K, TA.) ― -b4- And Eas~ato , (S, O, K,) aor. , (S, O, TA,) inf. n. Eas~N , (TA,) She (a camel) pastured alone. (S, O, K.) ― -b5- And Eas~a EalaY~a bixayorihi He was parsimonious to me with his wealth. (AA, TA.) -A3- Eas~ahu , (A,) aor. , (S, A,) inf. n. Eas~N ; (A;) and ↓ AEts~hu ; (S, * K, * TA;) He sought, or sought for or after, him [or it ]: (S, * A, K: *) or the latter, he sought, or sought for or after, it (a thing) by night. (TA.) You say, *ahaba yaEus~u SaAHibahu He went away seeking his companion. (A.) And AlA_ibila ↓ AiEotasasonaA walaA qisaAsFA ↓ famaA wajadonaA EisaAsFA We sought for the camels, or sought for them by night, and found not any trace. (TA.) And AlA=vaAra ↓ fulaAnN yaEotas~u Such a one traces footsteps. (A.) And ↓ yaEotas~u Alfujuwra He follows vice, immorality, or unrighteousness. (A.) -A4- Eas~a Alqawoma , (O, K,) aor. , inf. n. Eas~N , (TA,) He fed the people, or party, with somewhat little in quantity. (O, K, TA.)

EaSorN ; (S, Msb;) and ↓ AEtSrhu ; (S, O, Msb, K;) [ He pressed it, or squeezed it, so as to force out, i. e. he expressed, its juice, sirup, honey, oil, water, or moisture; ] he extracted, or fetched out by labour or art [i. e. by pressure or wringing ], (Msb, K,) its water, or juice, or the like, (Msb,) or what was in it, (K,) namely, what was in grapes, (S, Msb, K,) and the like, (Msb, K,) of things having oil, or sirup, or honey: (TA:) or EaSarahu signifies he performed that act himself; (K;) as also ↓ ES~rhu , inf. n. taEoSiyrN : (Sgh, TA:) or the latter, he superintended the pressing thereof, i. e., of grapes: (O:) and ↓ AEtSrhu , he had it done for him: (K:) or this last, he did it for another, or others: (Mgh, as implied by an explanation of muEotaSirN :) and EaSiyrFA ↓ AEtSr he prepared expressed juice or the like. (S, O.) [See also 8 below.] EuSora is used as a contraction of EuSira . (S, O.) ― -b2- [Hence,] EaSara Alv~awoba , inf. n. as above, He wrung out the water of the garment, or piece of cloth; he forced out its water by wringing it. (Msb.) ― -b3- And EaSara Ald~um~ala litaxoruja mid~atuhu [ He squeezed, or pressed, the pustule in order that its thick purulent matter might come forth ]. (Msb.) ― -b4- And EaSara Haloqahu [ He squeezed his throat ]. (Mgh and Msb in art. xnq .) ― -b5- And EaSara , aor. , (assumed tropical:) He took, or collected, the produce of the earth: from the same verb in the first of the senses expl. above: and hence, accord. to Abu-l-Ghowth, in the Kur [xii. 49], wafayhi yaEoSiruwna (assumed tropical:) And in it they shall take, or collect, the produce of the earth: (S:) or the meaning is, and in it they shall press grapes, or olives, or the like: or they shall milk the udders. (Bd.) [And there are other explanations, which see below.] -A2- EuSiruwA , (S, IKtt, O,) or ↓ A^uEoSiruwA , (O, K,) They were rained upon; they had rain; syn. muTiruwA , (S, O,) or A^umoTiruwA [which is less correct]. (TA.) [See AEtsr .] And biAlmaAli ↓ AEtSr AlEaS~aAru [or AlmaAla ? i. e. (tropical:) The extorter, or exacter, extorted, or exacted the property ]. AirotajaEa , (Mgh, O,) and Aisotarad~a . (Mgh.) Hence the trad. of 'Omar, AlwaAlidu yaEotaSiru waladahu fiymaA A^aEoTaAhu walayosa lilowaladi A^ano yaEotaSira mino waAlidihi , i. e., (tropical:) The father may take from his child what he has given him; [ but it is not for the child to take from his father what he has given him. ] (Mgh, O.) But as to the trad. of Esh-Shaabee, yaEotaSiru AlwaAlidu EalaY waladihi fiY maAlihi [(tropical:) The father may take back what he has given to his child ], the verb is made trans. by means of ElY because it implies the meaning of yarojiEu Ealayohi , and yaEuwdu Ealayohi : (IAth, Mgh, O: *) or this latter trad. means, the father may forbid his child his property, and withhold it from him: (S:) and [in like manner] the former trad., the father may withhold his child from giving his property, and forbid it to him: (TA:) for AEtSr also signifies he prevented, hindered, withheld, or refused; syn. manaEa . (TA.) [See AEtsr .] And biAlmaAli ↓ AEtSr AlEaS~aAru [or AlmaAla ? i. e. (tropical:) The extorter, or exacter, extorted, or exacted the property ]. AirotajaEa , (Mgh, O,) and Aisotarad~a . (Mgh.) sourceDefinition: [which is the most common form] and ↓ EuSurN (S, A, O, Msb, K) and ↓ EuSorN (S, A, O, K) and ↓ EiSorN (A, O, K) i. q. dahorN [as meaning Time; or a time; or a space or period of time ]; (S, A, O, Msb, K;) or any unlimited extent of time, during which peoples pass away and become extinct; (Esh-Shiháb, in the “ Sharh esh-Shifè; ”) [ a succession of ages: ] such is said by Fr to be its meaning in the Kur ciii. l: (TA:) pl. (of pauc., O) A^aEoSurN (O, K) and A^aEoSaArN ; (K;) and [of mult.] EuSuwrN (S, O, K) and EuSurN . (K.) You say, maA faEalotuhu EaSorFA , and biEaSorK , I did it not in its time. (A.) And ↓ jaA='u l`kin~a lamo yajiy^o liEuSorK He came, but he came not at the [ proper ] time of coming. (AZ, O, K: but AZ relates it without lkn~ . TA.) And ↓ naAma wamaA naAma liEuSorK , (K,) or, accord. to AZ and Sgh and the author of the L and others, mA ↓ nAm EuSorFA , (TA,) He slept, but hardly, or scarcely, slept. (AZ, K, &c.) And naAma fulaAnN walamo yanamo EaSorFA , and biEaSorK , Such a one slept, but slept not during a [ considerable period of ] time, or day; (A;) agreeably with other significations, here following. (TA.) ― -b2- EaSorN also signifies An hour, or a time, ( saAEapN ,) of the day. (Katádeh, O.) ― -b3- A day: (K:) [or day, as opposed to night: ] and a night: (K:) [or night, as opposed to day: ] also the morning, before, or after, sunrise; syn. gadaApN : and the afternoon; or evening; or last part of the day; until the sun becomes red; as also ↓ EaSarN , (IDrd, K.) Hence, AlEaSoraAni The night and the day: (O, TA:) or night and day: (Msb:) and the morning, before, or after, sunrise, and the afternoon or evening; or the first part of the day and the last part thereof: AlgadaApu waAlEa$iY~u . (ISk, S, O, Msb.) [See also AlA^aboradaAni .] A poet says, waA^amoTuluhu AlEaSorayoni Hat~aY yamal~uniY wayaroDaY biniSofi Ald~ayoni waAlA^anofu raAgimu [ And I put him off, delaying the payment of his debt, morning and evening, or from morning to evening, so that he loathes me, and is content with half of the debt, though unwilling ]: meaning, when he comes to me in the first part of the day, I promise to pay him in the last part of it: (ISk, S:) or, accord. to Sgh, the right reading (instead of wAlAnf rAgm ) is fiY gayori naAy^ili [ without liberality ]: and the verse is by 'Abd-Allah Ibn-Ez-Zubeyr El-Asadee. (TA.) ― -b4- Hence also (S, O) SalaApu AlEaSori , (S, O, Msb,) and ↓ SlAp AlEaSari , (O, TA,) fem. only, and simply AlEaSoru , [and ↓ AlEaSaru ,] mase. and fem., (Msb,) [ The prayer of afternoon; the time of which commences about mid-time between noon and nightfall; or accord. to the Shá- fi'ees, Málikees, and Hambelees, when the shade of an object, cast by the sun, is equal to the length of that object, added to the length of the shade which the same object casts at noon; and accord. to the Hanafees, when the shadow is equal to twice the length of the object added to the length of its mid-day shadow: its end being sunset, or the time when the sun becomes red:] so called because performed in one of the EaSoraAni , i. e., in the last portion of the day: (O:) also called AlS~alaApu AlwasoTaY [accord. to some], because it is between the two prayers of the day [that of daybreak and that of noon] and the two prayers of the night [that of sunset and that of nightfall]: (Abu-l-'Abbás:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aEoSurN ; and [of mult.] EuSuwrN . (Msb.) [And hence likewise,] AlEaSoraAni is applied in a trad. to The prayer of daybreak and that of the EaSor ; one being made predominant over the other; (Msb, TA;) as is the case in AlqamaraAni applied to the sun and the moon; (TA;) or they are so called because they are performed at the two extremities of the EaSoraAni , meaning the night and the day; (Msb, TA;) but the former is the more likely. (TA.) [See an ex. of the dim., AlEuSayoru , voce murohiqap , in art. rhq .] ― -b5- You say also, jaA='a fulaAnN EaSorFA , meaning Such a one came late. (Ks, S, O.) -A2- See also EaSiyrN . ― -b2- EaSorN also signifies (assumed tropical:) Rain from the [ clouds called ] muEoSiraAt . (K.) -A3- Also A man's [ near kinsfolk such as are termed his ] rahoT and Ea$iyrap : (O, K, * TA:) or his EaSabap [q. v.]. (TA.)

definition: A whirlwind of dust [or sand ], resembling a pillar;
sourceDefinition: A whirlwind of dust [or sand ], resembling a pillar; a wind that raises dust [or sand ] between the sky and the earth, and revolves, resembling a pillar; called also by the Arabs a zawobaEap ; of the masc. gender; (Msb;) a wind that raises the dust [or sand ], and rises towards the sky, as though it were a pillar; (S, O;) a wind that blows from the ground, (K, TA,) and raises the dust [or sand ], and rises (TA) like a pillar towards the sky; (K, TA;) called by the people a zawobaEap : (TA:) unless it blow in this manner, with vehemence, it is not thus called: (Zj, TA:) [see EamuwdN :] a wind that rises into the sky: (AZ:) or a wind that raises the clouds, (S, O, K,) with thunder and lightning: (S, O:) or in which is fire: (K:) mentioned in the Kur ii. 268: (S, O:) or in which is ↓ EiSaAr , which signifies vehement dust, (K,) or this latter word signifies dust raised into the air, by the wind, in the form of a pillar ( maA EaSarato bihi Alr~iyHu mina Alt~uraAbi fiY AlhawaA='i ): (TA:) [see also EaSarN :] pl. A^aEaASiyru , (Msb, TA,) and A^aEaASiru [occurring in poetry]. (Ham p. 678.) ― -b2- A_ino kunota riyHFA faqado laAqayota A_iEoSaArFA [ If thou be a wind, thou hast met with a whirlwind of dust like a pillar ] is a prov. of the Arabs, (O, TA,) relating to a man in whom is somewhat of power and who meets with one superior to him, (O,) or to a man who meets his adversary with courage. (TA.) ― -b3- And one says, waEoduhu A_iEoSaArN [ His promising is unprofitable like a whirlwind of dust ]. (A, TA.)

Ebs :) when you particularize him by a [proper] name, you say ↓ Eanobasapu , [i. e. The lion, ] making it imperfectly decl.; like as you say A^usaAmapu . (O, K.) (TA voce qasowarapN .)

(O.) ― -b2- AisotaEonadaniY mino bayoni Alqawomi He directed his course towards me, or sought me, [ singling me out ] from among the people, or party. (O, K. *) ― -b3- AstEnd said of a camel, and of a horse, He gained the mastery over the nose-rein, and over the halter, or leading-rope, (K, TA,) and resisted being led: (TA:) or AstEnd AlbaEiyru AlS~abiY~a the camel overcame the boy by gaining the mastery over the nose-rein, and dragged it, or him, along: and in like manner, AstEnd Alfarasu Alr~asana [ the horse gained the mastery over the halter, or leading-rope ]. (O, K, TA.)

definition: and ↓ EanodN and ↓ EunodN , (O, K,) accord.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ EanodN and ↓ EunodN , (O, K,) accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, (O,) i. q. naAHiyapN [app. as meaning The vicinage, or the quarter, tract, region, or place, of a person or thing]: (O, K:) whence the saying, huwa Einoda fulaAnK AlA=na [ He is in the vicinage, or the quarter, &c., of such a one, now ]. (O.) [See also EanadN , which has a similar meaning.] -A2- Einoda and ↓ Eanoda and ↓ Eunoda signify the same, (S, O, Msb, Mughnee, K,) being dial. vars., (S, O, Msb,) the first of which is the most common, (Mughnee,) and the most chaste: (Msb:) each is an adv. n. of place, and also of time; (S, O, Msb, Mughnee, K;) [used in the manner of a prep., though properly a prefixed noun;] of place when prefixed to a noun signifying a place [or anything local]; (TA;) of time when prefixed to a noun signifying a time: (Msb, TA:) denoting presence, (S, O,) i. e. perceptible presence, and also ideal presence, or rather the place of presence; (Mughnee;) and nearness, (S, O, Mughnee,) or the place of nearness; (Mughnee;) or the utmost nearness, and therefore it has no dim.; (T, TA;) [i. e.] it is primarily used in relation to that which is present with a person [or thing], in any adjacent part or quarter with respect to that person [or thing]; or in relation to that which is near to a person [or thing]: (Msb:) [thus it signifies At, near, nigh, by, near by, or close by, a place, or thing; with, present with, or in the presence of, a person or persons, or a thing or things; at the abode of a person; at the place of, or in the region of, a thing; or among, or amongst, persons or things: and at, near, nigh, or about, a time; and at, or on, or upon, denoting the occasion of an event or an action:] ― -b2- using it as an adv. n. of place, you say Einoda Albayoti [ At, near, nigh, by, near by, or close by, the house or tent ]; (TA;) and Einoda AlHaAy^iTi [ At, near, nigh, &c., the wall ]; (S, O;) [and EinodiY zayodN With me, present with me, in my presence, or at my abode, is Zeyd; and kunotu Einoda Alqawomi I was with, or among, the people, or party; and] falam~aA raA=hu musotaqir~FA Einodahu [ And when he saw it standing in his presence (in the Kur xxvii. 40)] is an ex. of its use as denoting presence perceptible by sense: and it is used as denoting nearness in the phrase Einoda sidorapi A@lomunotahaY [ Nigh to the lote-tree of the ultimate point of access (in the Kur liii. 14)]: (Mughnee:) you say also, EinodiY maAlN , meaning With me, or by me, i. e. present with me, is property; and meaning also in my possession, and in my power and at my disposal, is property, though absent from me; I have, or possess, property; (Msb, Mughnee; *) and liY Einodahu maAlN [ I have property in his hands, or possession; or there is property due to me in his hands, or possession; meaning, owed to me by him ]; as also qibalahu : (TA in art. qbl :) hence it is used in relation to attributes; so that one says, Einodahu xayorN wafaDolN [ He has, or possesses, goodness and excellence ]; and maA Enidahu $ar~N [ He has not evil ]: and hence the saying in the Kur [xxviii. 27], faA_ino A^atomamota Ea$orFA famino Einodika i. e. [ And if thou complete ten years, it will be] of thy redundant bounty; (Msb;) [or of thine own freewill; as is implied in the explanation by Bd, and agreeably with common usage:] and it is used as denoting ideal presence in the phrase qaAla A@l~a*iY Einodahu EilomN mina A@lokitaAbi [ He with whom was, i. e. who possessed, knowledge the of Scripture said (in the Kur xxvii. 40)]: (Mughnee:) [hence also] one says, liY Einoda fulaAnK HaAjapN [ I have an object of want to be sought, or required, at the hand of such a one, or a want to be supplied on the part of such a one; meaning I want a thing of such a one; as also qibala fulaAnK ]: (TA in art. Hwj :) [and in like manner one says of a right or due ( Haq~N ): and Talaba HaAjapF Einoda fulaAnK He sought an object of want at the hand of such a one: (see an ex. in art. Elw , conj. 3:)] ― -b3- using it as an adv. n. of time, you say Einoda AlS~uboHi [ At, near, nigh, or about, daybreak ]; (Msb, TA;) and Einoda All~ayoli [ At, near, nigh, or about, night ]; (S, O;) and jiy^otuka Einoda TuluwEi Al$~amosi [ I came to thee at, near, &c., the rising of the sun ]; (Mughnee;) [and Einoda *`lika At, on, upon, or on the occasion of, that event; thereupon; and EinodamaA faEala ka*aA At, on, upon, or on the occasion of, his doing such a thing. ] ― -b4- It admits before it the prep. mino , (S, O, Msb, Mughnee, K,) but no other prep.; (S, O, Msb;) like as does laduno : (S, O:) as in the saying, jiy^otu mino Einodihi [ I came from his presence, or his vicinage: or I came from him; for in this case it may be considered as redundant]: (Msb:) and in the saying A=tayonaAhu raHomapF mino EinodinaA waEal~amonaAhu mino ladun~aA EilomFA [ Upon whom we had bestowed mercy from us, and whom we had taught, from us, knowledge (in the Kur xviii. 64)]: (Mughnee:) [and in an ex. above, from the Kur xxviii. 27: and one says of a gift, h`*aA mino EinodiY , meaning This is from, or of, my property; or from me; or, by way of emphasis, from myself: ] one should not say [as the vulgar do], maDayotu A_ilaY Einodika ; nor A_ilaY ladunoka . (S, O, K. *) ― -b5- Being a vague adv. n., (T, TA,) it may not be used otherwise than as an adv. n., (T, S, O, K, TA,) except in the following case: (T, O, TA:) one says of a thing without knowing it, h`*aA EinodiY ka*aA [ This is in my judgment, or opinion, thus ]; and thereupon another says, A^awalaka EinodN [ And hast thou a judgment, or an opinion? ]: (T, A, * O, * K, * TA:) and in like manner one says, wamano A^anotumu Hat~aY yakuwna lakumo EinodN [ And who are ye, that ye should have a judgment, or an opinion? ]: (TA:) and thus in the saying, (Mughnee, TA,) of one of the Muwelleds, (Mughnee,) laA yusaAwiY niSofa Einodi kul~a EinodK laka EinodiY [ Every judgment, or opinion, of thine, in my judgment, or opinion, will not equal the half of a judgment, or an opinion ]: (Mughnee, TA:) they assert that Einod in this case means the mind, (T, O, * K, * TA,) i. e. Alqalob , and AlmaEoquwl , (O, K,) or Alqalob and maA fiyhi maEoquwlu All~ub~i ; (T, TA;) [as in the phrase buro liY maA Einoda fulaAnK , expl. in the S, in art. bwr , as meaning Try thou, or examine, and learn, for me, what is in the mind ( nafos ) of such a one; and in many other instances:] but this assertion is not valid: (T, TA:) [in a case of this kind] it means judgment [or opinion ]: thus one says, h`*aA EinodiY A^afoDalu mino h`*aA i. e. [ This is ] in my judgment [ more excellent than this ]: (Msb:) and A^anota EinodiY *aAhibN i. e. [ Thou art ] in my opinion [ going away ]: (Fr, Th, TA:) and h`*aA Alqawolu EinodiY SawaAbN [ This saying is in my judgment, or opinion, right, or correct ]: (Mughnee:) [and in like manner, Einoda A@ll~`hi is generally best rendered In the estimation, or sight, of God. ] ― -b6- [Sometimes it denotes comparison: see an ex. voce taEaAZama .] ― -b7- It is also sometimes used to denote incitement, (S, O, K,) being in this case prefixed [to ka or the like]; not alone: (MF:) yon say, Einodaka zayodFA , meaning Take thou Zeyd. (S, O, K.) ― -b8- And in cautioning a person respecting a thing before him, one says, Einodaka , [meaning Keep thou where thou art; and it is still used in this sense;] in which case it is an intrans. verbal noun. (Sb, L, TA.)

at the abode of a person; at the place of, or in the region of, a thing; or among, or amongst, persons or things: and at, near, nigh, or about, a time; and at, or on, or upon, denoting the occasion of an event or an action:] ― -b2- using it as an adv. n. of place, you say Einoda Albayoti [ At, near, nigh, by, near by, or close by, the house or tent ]; (TA;) and Einoda AlHaAy^iTi [ At, near, nigh, &c., the wall ]; (S, O;) [and EinodiY zayodN With me, present with me, in my presence, or at my abode, is Zeyd; and kunotu Einoda Alqawomi I was with, or among, the people, or party; and] falam~aA raA=hu musotaqir~FA Einodahu [ And when he saw it standing in his presence (in the Kur xxvii. 40)] is an ex. of its use as denoting presence perceptible by sense: and it is used as denoting nearness in the phrase Einoda sidorapi A@lomunotahaY [ Nigh to the lote-tree of the ultimate point of access (in the Kur liii. 14)]: (Mughnee:) you say also, EinodiY maAlN , meaning With me, or by me, i. e. present with me, is property; and meaning also in my possession, and in my power and at my disposal, is property, though absent from me; I have, or possess, property; (Msb, Mughnee; *) and liY Einodahu maAlN [ I have property in his hands, or possession; or there is property due to me in his hands, or possession; meaning, owed to me by him ]; as also qibalahu : (TA in art. qbl :) hence it is used in relation to attributes; so that one says, Einodahu xayorN wafaDolN [ He has, or possesses, goodness and excellence ]; and maA Enidahu $ar~N [ He has not evil ]: and hence the saying in the Kur [xxviii. 27], faA_ino A^atomamota Ea$orFA famino Einodika i. e. [ And if thou complete ten years, it will be] of thy redundant bounty; (Msb;) [or of thine own freewill; as is implied in the explanation by Bd, and agreeably with common usage:] and it is used as denoting ideal presence in the phrase qaAla A@l~a*iY Einodahu EilomN mina A@lokitaAbi [ He with whom was, i. e. who possessed, knowledge the of Scripture said (in the Kur xxvii. 40)]: (Mughnee:) [hence also] one says, liY Einoda fulaAnK HaAjapN [ I have an object of want to be sought, or required, at the hand of such a one, or a want to be supplied on the part of such a one; meaning I want a thing of such a one; as also qibala fulaAnK ]: (TA in art. Hwj :) [and in like manner one says of a right or due ( Haq~N ): and Talaba HaAjapF Einoda fulaAnK He sought an object of want at the hand of such a one: (see an ex. in art. Elw , conj. 3:)] ― -b3- using it as an adv. n. of time, you say Einoda AlS~uboHi [ At, near, nigh, or about, daybreak ]; (Msb, TA;) and Einoda All~ayoli [ At, near, nigh, or about, night ]; (S, O;) and jiy^otuka Einoda TuluwEi Al$~amosi [ I came to thee at, near, &c., the rising of the sun ]; (Mughnee;) [and Einoda *`lika At, on, upon, or on the occasion of, that event; thereupon; and EinodamaA faEala ka*aA At, on, upon, or on the occasion of, his doing such a thing. ] ― -b4- It admits before it the prep. mino , (S, O, Msb, Mughnee, K,) but no other prep.; (S, O, Msb;) like as does laduno : (S, O:) as in the saying, jiy^otu mino Einodihi [ I came from his presence, or his vicinage: or I came from him; for in this case it may be considered as redundant]: (Msb:) and in the saying A=tayonaAhu raHomapF mino EinodinaA waEal~amonaAhu mino ladun~aA EilomFA [ Upon whom we had bestowed mercy from us, and whom we had taught, from us, knowledge (in the Kur xviii. 64)]: (Mughnee:) [and in an ex. above, from the Kur xxviii. 27: and one says of a gift, h`*aA mino EinodiY , meaning This is from, or of, my property; or from me; or, by way of emphasis, from myself: ] one should not say [as the vulgar do], maDayotu A_ilaY Einodika ; nor A_ilaY ladunoka . (S, O, K. *) ― -b5- Being a vague adv. n., (T, TA,) it may not be used otherwise than as an adv. n., (T, S, O, K, TA,) except in the following case: (T, O, TA:) one says of a thing without knowing it, h`*aA EinodiY ka*aA [ This is in my judgment, or opinion, thus ]; and thereupon another says, A^awalaka EinodN [ And hast thou a judgment, or an opinion? ]: (T, A, * O, * K, * TA:) and in like manner one says, wamano A^anotumu Hat~aY yakuwna lakumo EinodN [ And who are ye, that ye should have a judgment, or an opinion? ]: (TA:) and thus in the saying, (Mughnee, TA,) of one of the Muwelleds, (Mughnee,) laA yusaAwiY niSofa Einodi kul~a EinodK laka EinodiY [ Every judgment, or opinion, of thine, in my judgment, or opinion, will not equal the half of a judgment, or an opinion ]: (Mughnee, TA:) they assert that Einod in this case means the mind, (T, O, * K, * TA,) i. e. Alqalob , and AlmaEoquwl , (O, K,) or Alqalob and maA fiyhi maEoquwlu All~ub~i ; (T, TA;) [as in the phrase buro liY maA Einoda fulaAnK , expl. in the S, in art. bwr , as meaning Try thou, or examine, and learn, for me, what is in the mind ( nafos ) of such a one; and in many other instances:] but this assertion is not valid: (T, TA:) [in a case of this kind] it means judgment [or opinion ]: thus one says, h`*aA EinodiY A^afoDalu mino h`*aA i. e. [ This is ] in my judgment [ more excellent than this ]: (Msb:) and A^anota EinodiY *aAhibN i. e. [ Thou art ] in my opinion [ going away ]: (Fr, Th, TA:) and h`*aA Alqawolu EinodiY SawaAbN [ This saying is in my judgment, or opinion, right, or correct ]: (Mughnee:) [and in like manner, Einoda A@ll~`hi is generally best rendered In the estimation, or sight, of God. ] ― -b6- [Sometimes it denotes comparison: see an ex. voce taEaAZama .] ― -b7- It is also sometimes used to denote incitement, (S, O, K,) being in this case prefixed [to ka or the like]; not alone: (MF:) yon say, Einodaka zayodFA , meaning Take thou Zeyd. (S, O, K.) ― -b8- And in cautioning a person respecting a thing before him, one says, Einodaka , [meaning Keep thou where thou art; and it is still used in this sense;] in which case it is an intrans. verbal noun. (Sb, L, TA.)

definition: The side [of a thing];

(L.)

definition: One who declines, or deviates, from the right way, or course;
sourceDefinition: One who declines, or deviates, from the right way, or course; (S, O, L;) as also ↓ EaniydN . (L.) See also EaAnidN as applied to a camel. ― -b2- A she-camel that deviates from the road by reason of her sprightliness and strength: pl. EunudN and Eun~adN ; or, as ISd thinks, this latter is pl. of ↓ EaAnidN , not of EanuwdN . (L.) ― -b3- A she-camel that pastures aside; (S, O;) that does not mix with the other camels, but removes to a distance from them, and always pastures aside; as also ↓ EaAnidN and EaAnidapN , (L;) that does not mix with the other camels, but is always apart from them; (IAth;) that is on one side of the other camels: (IAar and Aboo-Nasr:) pl. of the first EunudN ; (S, O, L;) and of the second and third, Eun~adN and EawaAnidu . (L.) ― -b4- A she-camel that continues to be opposite to the other camels, [or by their side; ] keeping pace with them: one that precedes them, or leads them, is termed saluwfN : so says El-Keysee: but accord. to ISd, EanuwdN is applied to a beast ( daAb~ap ), and to a wild ass, that precedes others in her pace. (L.) ― -b5- A man who alights in a place by himself, and mixes not with other persons. (A.) ― -b6- See also EaniydN . ― -b7- qidoHN EanuwdN [ An arrow of those used in the game called Almayosir ] that comes forth [ from the ribaAbap ] successful, in a direction, or manner, different from that of the other arrows. (O, L, K.) ― -b8- Eanuwdu Almirofaqi [A beast] having the elbow far from the zawor [or breast ]. (S, O, L.) ― -b9- EaqabapN EanuwdN [ A mountain road ] difficult of ascent. (L.) ― -b10- saHaAbapN EanuwdN (tropical:) A cloud abounding with rain: (O, L, K:) or that hardly removes from its place: (A:) pl. EunudN . (O, L.)

(S, O, K.) ― -b2- Hence, (A,) (tropical:) The depositary of one's secret [or secrets ]; (A, O, K) and it is used as a sing and a pl.:] one says, huwa Eayobapu fulaAn (tropical:) He is the depositary of the secret [or secrets of such a one: (A:) and it is said in a trad., AlA^anoSaAru kari$iY waEayobatiY (S, O, TA) (tropical:) The Anṣár are my intimates, and the depositary of my secret [or secrets ]. (TA. [See also other explanations in art. kr$ .]) And [in like manner] AlEyaAbu is used as meaning (tropical:) The breasts. and the hearts: (O, K:) for, as the Arab deposits in his Eyobap the best of his goods, or utensils, and of his clothes so he conceals in his breast his meat particular secrets, which may not be divulge. (O, * TA) Hence, (TA,) a poet says, wakaAdato EiyaAbu Alwud~i min~aA waminokumu waA_ino qiyla A^abonaA='u AlEumuwmapi taSofaru [ And our and your depositories of love, although it be said that we and you are the children of paternal uncles, were near to becoming and ]: (O, TA:) by EyAb Alwd~ he means their breasts. (TA.) And bayonanaA wabayonahumo EayobapN makofuwfapN , a phrase in the treaty of El-Hodeybiyeh. means (tropical:) Between us and them, in respect of this peace, is [determined that there shall be, in each party.] a breast bound to fulfil the terms of this writing. like the Eybp that is closed and fastened by its loops over its contents,] clear of secret enmity, and perfidy, and deceit: (IAar, O, * TA:) or, accord. to some, as related by Sh, evil between us [ and them ] shall be [as it were] tied up, like as the Eybp is tied up: or there shall be mutual reconciliation, and abstaining from war, like that kind of friendship that subsists between sincere friends who confide in each other. (Az, TA. [See also art. kf .]) ― -b3- Ealayoka biEayonatika , said by 'Áïsheh to 'Omar on an occasion of his blaming her, means (assumed tropical:) Busy thyself with thine own family, or wife, and let me alone. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (IDrd, S, O, L, Msb, K) and ↓ gudadapN (S, O, L, K) [ A ganglion; i. e.] any hard lump in the tendinous parts; (L, K;) [ a lump of ] flesh arising from disease, between the skin and the flesh, which may be made to move about: (Msb:) and any small nodous lump ( Euqodap ) in the body (IDrd, O, L, K) of a man, (IDrd, O, L,) surrounded by fat: (IDrd, O, L, K:) pl. gudadN [properly pl. of gud~apN , and also a coll. gen. n. of which gudadapN is the n. un.]: (S, O, L, Msb, K:) gud~apN [is applied in the present day to a ganglion: and a bubo: and a wen: and all these may be meant by its being said that it] also signifies a [ swelling such as is termed ] siloEap , (L, K,) overspread by fat. (L.) ― -b2- And gud~apN signifies likewise The plague, or pestilence, ( TaAEuwn ,) in camels; (As, S, O, L, K;) as also ↓ gadadN : (K:) or the same in camels as the TAEwn in man: (Msb:) it attacks them in the groins, and seldom do they recover from it: (L:) or it is only in the belly; (K, TA;) and when it extends to the camel's naHor [or part where he is stabbed, or stuck, when he is slaughtered], and to his groin, or arm-pit, the epithet daAbirN [so in the TA, but in the O daAriy^N , which I believe to be the right reading,] is applied to him: so says IAar: (TA:) or it is also in the fat parts; (Lth, O, L;) and between the flesh and the skin. (L.) ― -b3- And What is between the fat and the hump [of the camel]. (K.) -A2- Another signification of gud~apN is A part, or portion, of property; (L, K;) as in the saying, Ealayohi gud~apN mino maAlK [ He owes a part, or portion, of some property ]: (L:) pl. gadaAy^idu , (L, K,) and, in some of the copies of the K, gidaAdN . (TA.) And [these two pls.] gadaAy^idu and gidaAdN signify also Lots, portions, or shares: (L, K:) thus, accord. to Fr, the former of them means in a verse of Lebeed cited and expl. voce EadiydapN ; but the reading better known is EadaAy^idu : accord. to Az, gadaAy^idu in this instance signifies redundances. (L.)

sourceDefinition: A camel having the disease termed gud~apN ; (As, Az, S, O, L, K;) as also ↓ mugad~N (L) and ↓ magoduwdN , (Az, L, K,) or this is not said, (As, O, K,) but it was heard by Az from the Arabs, (O, L,) and ↓ mugad~adN (Az, L) and ↓ gaAd~N : (O, L, K:) mugid~N , without p , is also applied to a she-camel: and its pl. is magaAd~u : (L:) the pl. of ↓ gaAd~N is gidaA*N .
